akhfash:3-3.t: He said ﴿وَإِذَا كَالُوهُمْ أَوْ وَّزَنُوهُمْ يُخْسِرُونَ﴾, that is: "when they measure for people or weigh for them" (اذا كالوا الناس أَوْوَزَنُوهُم), because the people of the Hijaz say "كِلْتُ زَيْداً" and "وَزَنْتُه", meaning "I measured for him" (كِلْتُ لَهُ) and "I weighed for him" (وَزَنْتُ لَهُ).

akhfash:5-6.t: [And He said] ﴿لِيَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ﴾ ﴿يَوْمَ يَقُومُ ٱلنَّاسُ﴾: He placed it in (the sense of) "the time", as you say "فلانٌ اليومَ صالحٌ" ("So-and-so is well today"), meaning by it "now", at this time; and you say this at night: "فلانٌ اليومَ ساكِنٌ" ("So-and-so is calm today"), that is: now, that is: at this time. We know of no one who read it in the genitive, though the genitive is permissible.

akhfash:14-14.t: And He said ﴿كَلاَّ بَلْ رَانَ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾: you say of it "رانَ" "يَرِينُ" "رَيْناً" ("to cover over, rust over").

akhfash:28-28.t: And He said ﴿عَيْناً يَشْرَبُ بِهَا﴾: He made it dependent on ﴿يُسْقَوْنَ﴾ … ﴿عَيْناً﴾ ("they are given to drink … a spring"); and if you wish, you make it by way of praise (madḥ), cutting it off from the beginning of the statement, as if you said "I mean a spring" (أَعْنِي عَيْناً).

akhfash:36-36.t: And He said ﴿هَلْ ثُوِّبَ﴾: if you wish you assimilate (idghām), and if you wish you do not assimilate, because the lām's point of articulation is with the tip of the tongue, near the roots of the front teeth, and the thāʾ is with the tip of the tongue and the edges of the front teeth, except that the lām, on the right side, lies further inside the mouth. It is close to it in articulation, and that is why ﴿بَلْ تُؤْثِرُونَ﴾ was read with the lām assimilated into the tāʾ, because the point of articulation of tāʾ and thāʾ is close to that of the lām.

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ﴾ — and what has made you know — ﴿مَا عِلِّيُّونَ﴾: what is the record of ʿilliyyūn?

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿عَلَى الْأَرَائِكِ﴾: couches within canopied enclosures, ﴿يَنْظُرُونَ﴾ at the bliss they have been given.

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿تَعْرِفُ فِي وُجُوهِهِمْ نَضْرَةَ النَّعِيمِ﴾: the radiance of living in bliss and its beauty.

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿يُسْقَوْنَ مِنْ رَحِيقٍ﴾: wine pure of any impurity, ﴿مَخْتُومٍ﴾ upon its vessel, its seal broken by none but them.

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿خِتَامُهُ مِسْكٌ﴾, that is, the end of its drinking gives off the scent of musk. ﴿وَفِي ذَلِكَ فَلْيَتَنَافَسِ الْمُتَنَافِسُونَ﴾: so let them desire it by hastening to the obedience of Allah.

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿وَمِزَاجُهُ﴾, that is, what it is mixed with, ﴿مِنْ تَسْنِيمٍ﴾ — explained by His words:

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿عَيْنًا﴾: it is accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muqaddar) «أمدح» ("I praise"). ﴿يَشْرَبُ بِهَا الْمُقَرَّبُونَ﴾, that is, from it; or «يشرب» has been made to include the meaning of «يلتذ» ("to take delight").

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ أَجْرَمُوا﴾, such as Abū Jahl and his like, ﴿كَانُوا مِنَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾, such as ʿAmmār, Bilāl and their like, ﴿يَضْحَكُونَ﴾ in mockery of them.

celaleyn:30-30.t: ﴿وَإِذَا مَرُّوا﴾, that is, the believers, ﴿بِهِمْ يَتَغَامَزُونَ﴾, that is, the criminals signal to one another about the believers with the eyelid and the eyebrow in mockery.

celaleyn:31-31.t: ﴿وَإِذَا انْقَلَبُوا﴾: returned ﴿إِلَى أَهْلِهِمُ انْقَلَبُوا فَاكِهِينَ﴾ — in one reading [فَكِهِينَ] — delighted with their talk about the believers.

celaleyn:32-32.t: ﴿وَإِذَا رَأَوْهُمْ﴾, the believers, ﴿قَالُوا إِنَّ هَؤُلَاءِ لَضَالُّونَ﴾ because of their belief in Muhammad ﷺ. His words, Exalted is He:

celaleyn:33-33.t: ﴿وَمَا أُرْسِلُوا﴾, that is, the disbelievers, ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ — over the believers — ﴿حَافِظِينَ﴾ over them or over their deeds, so as to bring them back to what is in their interest.

celaleyn:34-34.t: ﴿فَالْيَوْمَ﴾, that is, the Day of Resurrection, ﴿الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنَ الْكُفَّارِ يَضْحَكُونَ﴾

celaleyn:35-35.t: ﴿عَلَى الْأَرَائِكِ﴾ in the Garden ﴿يَنْظُرُونَ﴾ from their dwellings at the disbelievers while they are being punished, and they laugh at them just as the disbelievers laughed at them in the world.

celaleyn:36-36.t: ﴿هَلْ ثُوِّبَ﴾ — been recompensed — ﴿الْكُفَّارُ مَا كَانُوا يَفْعَلُونَ﴾: Yes.

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿وَيْلٌ﴾ a word of punishment, or a valley in Hell, ﴿لِلْمُطَفِّفِينَ﴾

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ إِذَا اكْتَالُوا عَلَى﴾ i.e. from ﴿النَّاسِ يَسْتَوْفُونَ﴾ the measure in full,

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿وَإِذَا كَالُوهُمْ﴾ i.e. measured for them ﴿أَوْ وَزَنُوهُمْ﴾ i.e. weighed for them, ﴿يُخْسِرُونَ﴾ they reduce the measure or the weight.

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿أَلَا﴾ a question of rebuke; ﴿يَظُنُّ﴾ are certain ﴿أُولَئِكَ أَنَّهُمْ مَبْعُوثُونَ﴾

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿لِيَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ﴾ i.e. on it, and it is the Day of Resurrection,

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ a badal (substitute) for the position (maḥall) of لِيَوْمٍ, so what makes it accusative is مَبْعُوثُونَ; ﴿يَقُومُ النَّاسُ﴾ from their graves ﴿لِرَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ the creatures, for the sake of His command, His reckoning and His recompense?

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾ truly ﴿إِنَّ كِتَابَ الْفُجَّارِ﴾ i.e. the record of the deeds of the unbelievers ﴿لَفِي سِجِّينٍ﴾ it is said: it is a book gathering the deeds of the devils and the unbelievers; and it is said: it is a place beneath the seventh earth, and it is the abode of Iblīs and his troops.

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا سِجِّينٌ﴾ what the book of Sijjīn is?

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here]

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ يُكَذِّبُونَ بِيَوْمِ الدِّينِ﴾ the Recompense; a badal (substitute) or an explanation (bayān) of لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ.

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿وَمَا يُكَذِّبُ بِهِ إِلَّا كُلُّ مُعْتَدٍ﴾ who oversteps the limit, ﴿أَثِيمٍ﴾ an intensive form (ṣīghat mubālagha),

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿إِذَا تُتْلَى عَلَيْهِ آيَاتُنَا﴾ the Quran ﴿قَالَ أَسَاطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ the tales that were written down in ancient times; plural of أُسْطُورَة with ḍamma, or إِسْطَارَة with kasra.

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾ a deterrent and rebuke for their saying that; ﴿بَلْ رَانَ﴾ has overcome ﴿عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾ and covered them ﴿مَا كَانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ﴾ of sins, so it is like rust.

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾ truly ﴿إِنَّهُمْ عَنْ رَبِّهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ on the Day of Resurrection ﴿لَمَحْجُوبُونَ﴾ so they will not see Him.

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿ثُمَّ إِنَّهُمْ لَصَالُوا الْجَحِيمِ﴾ will surely enter the burning Fire.

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿ثُمَّ يُقَالُ﴾ to them: ﴿هَذَا﴾ i.e. the punishment ﴿الَّذِي كُنْتُمْ بِهِ تُكَذِّبُونَ﴾

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾ truly ﴿إِنَّ كِتَابَ الْأَبْرَارِ﴾ i.e. the record of the deeds of the believers who are truthful in their faith ﴿لَفِي عِلِّيِّينَ﴾ it is said: it is a book gathering the good deeds of the angels and of the believers among the two weighty races (al-thaqalayn); and it is said: it is a place in the seventh heaven beneath the Throne.

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿وَيْلٌ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ); ﴿لِلْمُطَفِّفِينَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: badal (substitute) for المطففين; ﴿إِذَا﴾: a conditional adverb that does not put the verb in the jussive; ﴿اكْتالُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); ﴿عَلَى النَّاسِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what precedes them; ﴿يَسْتَوْفُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its agent; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿وَإِذا﴾: conjoined to the first إذا; ﴿كالُوهُمْ﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its object; the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); ﴿أَوْ﴾: a conjunction; ﴿وَزَنُوهُمْ﴾: conjoined to كالوهم. ﴿يُخْسِرُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its agent; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿أَلا﴾: the hamza is an interrogative particle and ﴿لا﴾ is negative; ﴿يَظُنُّ﴾: an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ); ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾: fāʿil (agent); ﴿أَنَّهُمْ مَبْعُوثُونَ﴾: anna, its noun and its khabar (predicate); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from anna and what follows it stands in place of the two objects of يظن.

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿لِيَوْمٍ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) مبعوثون; ﴿عَظِيمٍ﴾: naʿt (adjective).

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿يَوْمَ﴾: an adverb of time; ﴿يَقُومُ النَّاسُ﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); ﴿لِرَبِّ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿الْعالَمِينَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾: a particle of deterrence and rebuke; ﴿إِنَّ كِتابَ﴾: inna and its noun, muḍāf to ﴿الفُجَّارِ﴾, which is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿لَفِي﴾: the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); ﴿في سِجِّينٍ﴾: the khabar (predicate) of inna; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is a resumptive particle and ﴿ما﴾ is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿أَدْراكَ﴾: a past verb and its object, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿ما سِجِّينٌ﴾: mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the clause stands in place of the second object of أدراك.

daas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿كِتابٌ﴾: badal (substitute) for سجين; ﴿مَرْقُومٌ﴾: naʿt (adjective) of كتاب.

daas-irab:10-10.t: ﴿وَيْلٌ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾: an adverb of time annexed to one like it; ﴿لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ﴾: the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: naʿt (adjective) of المكذبين; ﴿يُكَذِّبُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين; ﴿بِيَوْمِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿الدِّينِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

daas-irab:12-12.t: ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) and ﴿ما﴾ is negative; ﴿يُكَذِّبُ﴾: an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ); ﴿بِهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿كُلُّ﴾: fāʿil (agent), muḍāf to ﴿مُعْتَدٍ﴾; ﴿أَثِيمٍ﴾: naʿt (adjective); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:13-13.t: ﴿إِذا﴾: a conditional adverb that does not put the verb in the jussive; ﴿تُتْلى﴾: a passive imperfect verb; ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿آياتُنا﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿قالَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) and has no grammatical position; ﴿أَساطِيرُ﴾: khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the nominal clause is the maqūl (speech content) of the saying.

daas-irab:14-14.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾: a particle of deterrence and rebuke; ﴿بَلْ﴾: a particle of transition and digression (iḍrāb); ﴿رانَ﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa; ﴿عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿ما﴾: the fāʿil (agent) of ران; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿كانُوا﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, the wāw being its noun; ﴿يَكْسِبُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its agent; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of kāna, and the clause كانوا… is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما.

daas-irab:15-15.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾: a particle of deterrence and rebuke; ﴿إِنَّهُمْ﴾: inna and its noun; ﴿عَنْ رَبِّهِمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate); ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾: an adverb of time annexed to one like it; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position; ﴿لَمَحْجُوبُونَ﴾: the khabar, with the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa).

daas-irab:16-16.t: ﴿ثُمَّ﴾: a conjunction; ﴿إِنَّهُمْ﴾: inna and its noun, and the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); ﴿صالوا﴾: the khabar (predicate) of inna, nominative (marfūʿ) by the wāw, the nūn having been dropped for annexation (iḍāfa); ﴿الْجَحِيمِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:17-17.t: ﴿ثُمَّ﴾: a conjunction; ﴿يُقالُ﴾: a passive imperfect verb, its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) being latent (mustatir); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿هذَا الَّذِي﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾: kāna and its noun; ﴿بِهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what follows them; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿تُكَذِّبُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ) and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the khabar of كنتم.

daas-irab:18-18.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾: a particle of deterrence and rebuke; ﴿إِنَّ كِتابَ﴾: inna and its noun, muḍāf to ﴿الْأَبْرارِ﴾, which is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿لَفِي﴾: the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); ﴿في عِلِّيِّينَ﴾: the khabar (predicate) of inna; the clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:20-20.t: Parsed like verse no. 9; مرقوم is an adjective of كتاب.

daas-irab:21-21.t: ﴿يَشْهَدُهُ﴾: an imperfect verb and its object; ﴿الْمُقَرَّبُونَ﴾: fāʿil (agent); the clause is a second naʿt (adjective) of كتاب.

daas-irab:22-22.t: ﴿إِنَّ الْأَبْرارَ﴾: inna and its noun; ﴿لَفِي﴾: the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); ﴿في نَعِيمٍ﴾: the khabar (predicate) of inna; the clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:23-23.t: ﴿عَلَى الْأَرائِكِ﴾: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) what follows them; ﴿يَنْظُرُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:24-24.t: ﴿تَعْرِفُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿فِي وُجُوهِهِمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿نَضْرَةَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), muḍāf to ﴿النَّعِيمِ﴾; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:25-25.t: ﴿يُسْقَوْنَ﴾: a passive imperfect verb, the wāw being the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); ﴿مِنْ رَحِيقٍ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿مَخْتُومٍ﴾: naʿt (adjective); the clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:26-26.t: ﴿خِتامُهُ مِسْكٌ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the clause is a second naʿt (adjective) of رحيق. ﴿وَفِي﴾: the wāw is a resumptive particle; ﴿فِي ذلِكَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what follows them; ﴿فَلْيَتَنافَسِ﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the lām of command; ﴿الْمُتَنافِسُونَ﴾: fāʿil (agent); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:27-27.t: ﴿وَمِزاجُهُ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and a mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿مِنْ تَسْنِيمٍ﴾: its khabar (predicate); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:28-28.t: ﴿عَيْناً﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "أمدح" (I praise); ﴿يَشْرَبُ﴾: an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ); ﴿بِهَا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿الْمُقَرَّبُونَ﴾: postponed fāʿil (agent); the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of عينا.

daas-irab:29-29.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ﴾: inna and its noun; ﴿أَجْرَمُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين; ﴿كانُوا﴾: kāna and its noun; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the clause إن الذين… is resumptive; ﴿مِنَ الَّذِينَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) يضحكون; ﴿آمَنُوا﴾: a past verb and its agent; the clause is the ṣila of الذين; ﴿يَضْحَكُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb and its agent; the clause is the khabar of كانوا.

daas-irab:30-30.t: ﴿وَإِذا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿إِذا﴾: a conditional adverb that does not put the verb in the jussive; ﴿مَرُّوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿بِهِمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿يَتَغامَزُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its agent; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:31-31.t: ﴿وَإِذَا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿إِذَا﴾: a conditional adverb that does not put the verb in the jussive; ﴿انْقَلَبُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿إِلى أَهْلِهِمُ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what precedes them; the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); ﴿انْقَلَبُوا﴾: a past verb and its agent; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) and has no grammatical position; ﴿فَكِهِينَ﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:32-32.t: ﴿وَإِذا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿إِذا﴾: a conditional adverb that does not put the verb in the jussive; ﴿رَأَوْهُمْ﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its object; the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); ﴿قالُوا﴾: a past verb and its agent; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) and has no grammatical position. ﴿إِنَّ هؤُلاءِ لَضالُّونَ﴾: inna and its noun, and the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); ﴿لَضالُّونَ﴾: the khabar (predicate) of inna; the clause is the maqūl (speech content) of the saying.

daas-irab:33-33.t: ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); ﴿ما﴾: negative; ﴿أُرْسِلُوا﴾: a passive past verb, the wāw being the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿حافِظِينَ﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause is a ḥāl.

daas-irab:34-34.t: ﴿فَالْيَوْمَ﴾: the fāʾ is a resumptive particle and ﴿اليوم﴾ is an adverb of time; ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿آمَنُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿مِنَ الْكُفَّارِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what follows them; ﴿يَضْحَكُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its agent; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:35-35.t: ﴿عَلَى الْأَرائِكِ﴾: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) what follows them; ﴿يَنْظُرُونَ﴾: the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:36-36.t: ﴿هَلْ﴾: an interrogative particle; ﴿ثُوِّبَ﴾: a passive past verb; ﴿الْكُفَّارُ﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the maqūl (speech content) of an omitted verb of saying; ﴿ما﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿كانُوا﴾: kāna and its noun; ﴿يَفْعَلُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of كانوا, and the clause كانوا is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما.

dervis-irab:1-13.t:
* Vocabulary:
(لِلْمُطَفِّفِينَ) التطفيف: short-changing in measure and weight, because what is withheld is something slight (طفيف) and paltry. طفف المكيال: he diminished the measure slightly. Al-Zajjāj said: "The one who diminishes the measure and the balance was called مطفف only because he hardly steals from the measure and the balance anything but a small, slight amount."
(اكْتالُوا) Al-Farrāʾ said: one says اكتلت على الناس: I took full measure from them; and اكتلت منهم: I took what was due from them; so على has the meaning of من.
(سِجِّينٍ) Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: Allah has reported of the record of the wicked that it is in سجين, and has explained سجين as a written record, so it is as though it were said: their record is in a written record — what does that mean? I say: سجين is a comprehensive book; it is the register of evil, in which Allah has recorded the deeds of the devils and the deeds of the disbelievers and the corrupt among jinn and humans. It is a written record, inscribed and clearly written, or marked, so that whoever sees it knows there is no good in it. So the meaning is that what is written of the deeds of the wicked is established in that register. It was named سجين, a faʿīl from السجن, which is imprisonment and constriction, because it is a cause of imprisonment and constriction in Hell," until he says: "If you say: what is سجين — is it an adjective or a noun? I say: rather, it is a proper noun transferred from an adjective, like حاتم, and it is triptote, because there is only one cause [of diptosis] in it, namely definiteness."
Abū Ḥayyān's wording: "As for سجين, the majority said it is a fiʿʿīl from السجن, like سكير; or in place of ساجن, so it came as an intensive form; on this view سجين is an adjective of an omitted place. Ibn Muqbil said:
ورفقة يضربون البيض ضاحية ... ضربا تواصت به الأبطال سجينا
(And a band of companions striking the helmets in broad daylight, with a lasting, severe blow which the heroes enjoined one another.)"
Then he cited what al-Zamakhsharī said, and said: "They differed over سجين, if it is a place, in a confused disagreement whose mention we have omitted. The apparent sense is that سجين is a book, and that is why كتاب مرقوم was made a badal (substitute) from it. ʿIkrima said: سجين is an expression for loss and abasement, as you say 'So-and-so has reached rock bottom' when he has become utterly inert. Some lexicographers said: the nūn of سجين is a substitute for a lām, and it is from السجل (the register). It is thus summarized from their statements that the nūn of سجين is either radical or a substitute for a lām; if it is radical, its derivation is from السجن."
The author of al-Qāmūs cited under the root سجن the following text: "And [سجين], like سكين: the lasting, the severe; a place in which is the record of the wicked; a valley in Hell — may Allah the Exalted protect us from it; or a rock in the seventh earth."
(مَرْقُومٌ) written, inscribed. The basic meaning of الرقم is writing; and from it is the poet's saying:
سأرقم في الماء القراح إليكم ... على بعدكم إن كان للماء راقم
(I shall write to you on clear water, despite your distance, if water has anyone who can write on it.)

* I'rab:
(وَيْلٌ لِلْمُطَفِّفِينَ) (ويل) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); what licenses beginning with it is its being an imprecation; and (للمطففين) is its khabar (predicate). Had it been accusative, that would have been permissible. It has been said: "The preferred form for ويل and its like, when it is not in a genitive construct, is the nominative, and the accusative is permissible; if it is in a construct or made definite, the preferred form is the accusative, as in ويلكم لا تغترّوا."
(الَّذِينَ إِذَا اكْتالُوا عَلَى النَّاسِ يَسْتَوْفُونَ) (الذين) is an adjective of (المطففين). (إذا) is an adverb for future time containing the meaning of condition, attached (mutaʿalliq) to the omitted apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), its implied form being "they took from them". The clause (اكتالوا) is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it. (على الناس) is attached to (اكتالوا); it has also been said that it is attached to (يستوفون), the object having been placed before the verb only to convey specificity. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Since their taking measure was a taking of measure that harmed [people] and in which they were imposed upon, على was substituted in place of من to indicate that. It may also be attached to يستوفون, the object being placed before the verb to convey specificity, i.e. they take full measure from people in particular; as for themselves, they take full measure for them." Ibn Hishām made «على» mean «من», agreeing in that with al-Zamakhsharī. The clause (يستوفون) is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of the omitted apodosis, i.e. they took from them, taking full measure.
(وَإِذا كالُوهُمْ أَوْ وَزَنُوهُمْ يُخْسِرُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction. (إذا) is an adverb for future time attached to the omitted apodosis, its implied form being "they took full measure for it". The clause (كالوهم) is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it. (كالوهم) is a past verb and its fāʿil, and the hāʾ [i.e. هم] is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. they measured the food out for them. (أو) is a conjunction, and (وزنوهم) is conjoined to (كالوهم) and parsed in parallel with it. Al-Zamakhsharī's wording: "The pronoun in كالوهم أو وزنوهم is an accusative pronoun referring to الناس, and there are two views on it: that what is meant is كالوا لهم أو وزنوا لهم, with the preposition omitted and the verb joined directly, as he said:
ولقد جنيتك أكمؤا وعساقلا ... ولقد نهيتك عن نبات الأوبر
(I gathered truffles and ʿasāqil for you, and I forbade you the daughters of Awbar.)"
جنى is transitive only to one object, and to the second by means of the lām; so the original is جنيت لك, with the preposition omitted and the pronoun joined directly; or it was made to include (taḍmīn) the meaning of انجتك [Translator's note: so in the source; apparently a corruption of a verb such as أجنيتك or أنلتك] and so made transitive to both. الأكمؤ is the plural of كمء, like أفلس; it is the singular of الكمأة, which is a large kind of plant called "the fat of the earth"; it was called كمأة because of its being known by it. العساقل is the plural of عسقول, like عصفور; its due form was عساقيل, but the yāʾ was dropped for the metre. It has been said that it is the plural of عسقل, which is a small, good, white kind of it. بنات أوبر are a poor, black, downy kind of it, as though it had fur on it; it has been said that it is a species resembling colocasia or turnip. بنات أوبر is the plural of ابن أوبر, because it is a proper name for something non-rational, and the al in it is redundant (zāʾida). Al-Mubarrad said: it is a generic noun. The verse is of the type of allegory (tamthīl) for the state of one who was urged towards the good but turned aside to the bad, then came back regretting its outcome. We return to what we are about, and say: among examples of what is accusative by removal of the preposition is their saying الحريص يصيدك لا الجواد ("the eager one catches for you, not the steed"), the original being يصيد لك. What has been said, that هم is a nominative pronoun emphasizing the wāw in (كالوهم), is a mistake. (أو) is a conjunction, and (وزنوهم) is conjoined to (كالوهم); the same is said in its parsing as was said about (كالوهم), i.e. وزنوا لهم. Abū Ḥayyān's wording: "كال and وزن are among the verbs made transitive by a preposition; so you say كلت لك and وزنت لك, and the lām may be omitted, as in your saying نصحت لك and نصحتك, شكرت لك and شكرتك. The pronoun is an accusative pronoun, i.e. كالوا لهم ووزنوا لهم, with the preposition omitted and the verb joined by itself; and the object, which is what is measured or weighed, is omitted." The clause (يخسرون) is a ḥāl from the omitted apodosis.
(أَلا يَظُنُّ أُولئِكَ أَنَّهُمْ مَبْعُوثُونَ لِيَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ يَوْمَ يَقُومُ النَّاسُ لِرَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ) The hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval, (لا) is negative, and (يظن) is an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ). الظن here means certainty, i.e. are those not certain? Had they been certain, they would not have diminished the measure and the weight. (أولئك) is the fāʿil, the reference being to those who give short measure. (أنّ) with what is in its scope stands in place of the two objects of (يظن). (أنّ) and its noun; (مبعوثون) is its khabar; and (ليوم) is attached to (مبعوثون), or it is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, and it is indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa only because of its annexation to the verb [Translator's note: this remark evidently refers to the alternative of (يوم يقوم) being in the nominative position yet ending in fatḥa; it is so placed in the source]. (عظيم) is a naʿt (adjective). (يوم) is a badal from (ليوم), following it in position; its position is accusative by the mentioned (مبعوثون) or by an implied verb like it, because the badal is on the intention of repeating the governor. The clause (يقوم الناس) is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it, and (لرب العالمين) is attached to (يقوم). It is reported of Ibn ʿUmrān [Translator's note: so in the source; the report is known of Ibn ʿUmar] that he recited this sūra, and when he reached His saying يوم يقوم الناس لرب العالمين he wept aloud and was unable to recite what came after it. It is reported of ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān that a Bedouin said to him: "You have heard what Allah said about those who give short measure" — by that he meant: the one who gives short measure has had this tremendous threat, which you have heard, directed at him; so what do you think of yourself, when you take the wealth of the Muslims without measure or weight?
(كَلَّا إِنَّ كِتابَ الفُجَّارِ لَفِي سِجِّينٍ وَما أَدْراكَ ما سِجِّينٌ كِتابٌ مَرْقُومٌ) (كلا) is a rebuke and restraint for them from giving short measure and from heedlessness of the Reckoning and the Resurrection. (إنّ) and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); and (في سجين) is the khabar of (إنّ). (ما) is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ, and the clause (أدراك) is the khabar. (ما) is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ, and (سجين) is the khabar; the nominal clause, suspended (muʿallaqa) by the interrogative, stands in place of the second object of (أدراك). (كتاب) is a badal from (سجين), or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is a written record"; and (مرقوم) is an adjective of (كتاب). If (سجين) is considered the name of a place, then the khabar reading is preferable, or one assumes an annexed noun omitted before (سجين), so as to ward off the objection: سجين is the name of a place, so how can it be explained as a written record?
(وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ الَّذِينَ يُكَذِّبُونَ بِيَوْمِ الدِّينِ) (ويل) is a mubtadaʾ, as has preceded; (يومئذ) is an adverb annexed to its like, attached to (ويل); (للمكذبين) is the khabar; (الذين) is a naʿt of (المكذبين); the clause (يكذبون) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of (الذين); and (بيوم الدين) is attached to (يكذبون).
(وَما يُكَذِّبُ بِهِ إِلَّا كُلُّ مُعْتَدٍ أَثِيمٍ) The wāw is a conjunction or circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (ما) is negative; (يكذب) is an imperfect verb in the nominative; (به) is attached to (يكذب); (إلا) is a particle of restriction; and (كل معتد أثيم) is the fāʿil of (يكذب).
(إِذا تُتْلى عَلَيْهِ آياتُنا قالَ أَساطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ) (إذا) is a future adverb containing the meaning of condition, attached to its apodosis, which is (قال). The clause (تتلى) is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it; (عليه) is attached to (تتلى); and (آياتنا) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of (تتلى). The clause (قال) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of (إذا). (أساطير الأولين) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. هي. It has preceded that الأساطير is the plural of أسطورة or أساطرة [Translator's note: so in the source; usually given as إسطارة], with kasra, which is a tale written down long ago.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «الذين إذا اكتالوا على الناس يستوفون وإذا كالوهم أو وزنوهم يخسرون» there is antithesis (muqābala), which came in the finest and most orderly way: i.e. when the measuring is on the part of others, they take it in full, and when the measuring is on their own part in particular, they make it deficient, whether they carry it out themselves or not. The pronoun does not indicate carrying out personally, nor does it hint at that. What shows you that the pronoun does not convey carrying out the act personally is that you may say: "The rulers are the ones who carry out the prescribed punishments, not the common people," and you do not mean that they carry it out themselves; its meaning is only that doing that is on their part in particular. It has been said that the people of Medina were merchants who gave short measure, and their sales were al-munābadha [Translator's note: the source prints المنابزة, for المنابذة], al-mulāmasa and al-mukhāṭara (forms of gambling sales). So it was revealed, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out and recited it to them and said: "Five for five." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is five for five?" He said: "No people break the covenant but Allah sets their enemy over them; they do not judge by other than what Allah has revealed but poverty spreads among them; indecency does not appear among them but death spreads among them; they do not give short measure but they are denied vegetation and seized with years of famine; and they do not withhold the zakāt but rain is held back from them." It has also been said that it was revealed about a man known as Abū Juhayna who had two ṣāʿ-measures: he measured out with one and took measure with the other, i.e. he took with one and gave with the other.

dervis-irab:14-36.t:
* Vocabulary:
(رانَ): it overcame, encompassed and covered, as clouds cover the sky. In al-Mukhtār: "al-rayn is the seal and the filth. One says rāna dhanbuhu ʿalā qalbihi (his sin overlaid his heart), of the pattern bāʿa (rāna yarīnu); and rayūnan also means it overcame." Abū ʿUbayda said: "Whatever overcomes you has rāna bika, rānaka and rāna ʿalayka. A man is rīna when he falls into something he cannot get out of and has no power over." Al-Zamakhsharī's wording: "﴿رانَ عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾: it mounted them as rust mounts, and overcame them. That is, he persists in major sins and keeps postponing repentance until his heart is sealed, so that it neither accepts good nor inclines to it. On the authority of al-Ḥasan: it is sin upon sin until the heart turns black. One says rāna ʿalayhi al-dhanb and ghāna ʿalayhi, rayn and ghayn; and al-ghayn is cloud. One says rāna fīhi al-nawm (sleep settled deep in him), and rānat bihi al-khamr (wine carried him away)." I say: rāna is of the yāʾ-type and the wāw-type; here it is of the yāʾ-type. One says rāna yarīnu raynan and rayūnan, said of a thing, such a person, "upon him" and "with him": it overcame him. You say rāna hawāhu ʿalā qalbihi, i.e. his desire overcame it; rānat nafsuhu: his soul became foul and clouded over; rāna al-mawt ʿalayhi and bihi: death took him away; rīna bihi: he fell into what he cannot get out of and has no strength for, and died, and fell into distress; arāna, irānatan, of a people: their cattle perished, so they are murīnūn. Al-rān is a shoe like the khuff but longer. Al-rayna is wine, because it overcomes the intellect.
As for the wāw-type, one says rāna yarūnu raunan (of the pattern dakhala) of a matter: it became severe; rānat al-layla: its terror or gloom became severe. Al-raun (with a doubled, damma-vowelled rāʾ) is hardship, plural ruʾūn; rawnat al-shayʾ (with damma) is its greater part and its severity. One says "may Allah remove from you the rawna of this matter," i.e. its severity and gloom. Al-arūnān means the hard thing. One says al-arūnān and al-arūnānī for what is severe in anything: heat, cold, uproar, shouting, grief and joy; its feminine is arūnāna and arūnāniyya.
(عِلِّيُّونَ): Al-Zamakhsharī said: "ʿIlliyyūn is a proper name for the register of good in which is recorded everything that the angels and the righteous of the two weighty races (jinn and mankind) have done. It is transferred from the plural of ʿilliyy, a faʿīl form from al-ʿulūw (height), like sijjīn from al-sijn. It was so named either because it is the cause of ascent to the highest degrees in Paradise, or because it is raised up in the seventh heaven where the cherubim dwell, in honour and veneration of it." Abū Ḥayyān's wording: ʿilliyyūn is a plural whose singular is ʿilliyy, derived from al-ʿulūw, being an intensive form; this was said by Yūnus and Ibn Jinnī. Abū al-Fatḥ said: the proper form would be ʿilliyya, as they call the upper room ʿilliyya; when the tāʾ was dropped they compensated for it with the plural in wāw and nūn. It was also said that it is a description of the angels, which is why it is pluralised with wāw and nūn. Al-Farrāʾ said: it is a noun set down on the plural pattern, with no singular from its own wording, like ʿishrīn and thalāthīn; when the Arabs form a plural that has no singular pattern and no dual, they use wāw and nūn for both masculine and feminine. Al-Zajjāj said: this noun is declined like the plural: "this is Qinnasrūn" and "I saw Qinnasrīn." Ibn Hishām said in the discussion of what is attached to the sound masculine plural: "The fourth is what is used as a name from these plurals and what is attached to it, such as ʿilliyyūn," that is, it is attached to this plural and is used as a name for the highest part of Paradise. Al-Rāghib said: it was said to be the name of the noblest of the gardens, just as sijjīn is the noblest of the fires; and it was said that in reality it is the name of its inhabitants, which is closer to Arabic since this plural is specific to rational beings and the singular is ʿilliyy; its meaning is that the righteous are among these.

* I'rab:
(كَلَّا بَلْ رانَ عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ ما كانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ): كلا is a particle of rebuke and reproof to the sinful transgressor against that false statement, and a denial of him in it; بل is a conjunction and particle of rejection (iḍrāb); رانَ is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa; عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ is attached to رانَ; ما is the agent (fāʿil); the clause كانُوا is a clause with no grammatical position because it is a ṣila; كان and its subject, and the clause يَكْسِبُونَ is the predicate of كانُوا. (كَلَّا إِنَّهُمْ عَنْ رَبِّهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ لَمَحْجُوبُونَ): كلا is likewise a particle of rebuke and reproof against the earning that has overlaid their hearts; إن and its noun; عَنْ رَبِّهِمْ is attached to مَحْجُوبُونَ; يَوْمَئِذٍ is an adverbial (ẓarf) annexed to its like, also attached to مَحْجُوبُونَ; مَحْجُوبُونَ is the predicate of إن; the tanwīn in إذ is a compensation for a clause whose implied form is "on the day when the people rise". The meaning of "veiled" will come under the section on Rhetoric. (ثُمَّ إِنَّهُمْ لَصالُوا الْجَحِيمِ): ثم is a conjunction denoting distance in rank, for burning in Hell is worse than humiliation and deprivation of mercy and honour; إن and its noun; the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); صالُوا الْجَحِيمِ is the predicate of إن. (ثُمَّ يُقالُ هذَا الَّذِي كُنْتُمْ بِهِ تُكَذِّبُونَ): ثم is a conjunction denoting sequence and distance as well; يُقالُ is an imperfect passive verb, and the deputy agent (nāʾib fāʿil) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he"; هذا is a mubtadaʾ and الَّذِي its khabar; the clause كُنْتُمْ is a ṣila; كان and its subject; بِهِ is attached to تُكَذِّبُونَ, and the clause تُكَذِّبُونَ is the predicate of كُنْتُمْ. (كَلَّا إِنَّ كِتابَ الْأَبْرارِ لَفِي عِلِّيِّينَ وَما أَدْراكَ ما عِلِّيُّونَ): كلا is an emphasis of the rebuke and of the obligation to desist; إن and its noun; the shifted lām; فِي عِلِّيِّينَ is its predicate, and the sign of the genitive in عِلِّيِّينَ is the yāʾ in place of the kasra because it is attached to the sound masculine plural; the wāw is a conjunction; ما is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ, and the clause أَدْراكَ is its khabar; ما is an interrogative noun for magnification and exaltation, mubtadaʾ, and عِلِّيُّونَ is the khabar, its sign of nominative being the wāw in place of the damma because it is attached to the sound masculine plural; the clause suspended by the interrogative fills the place of the second object of أَدْراكَ. (كِتابٌ مَرْقُومٌ يَشْهَدُهُ الْمُقَرَّبُونَ): كِتابٌ is a badal of عِلِّيُّونَ, or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, which is preferable; مَرْقُومٌ is an adjective (naʿt) of كِتابٌ, and the clause يَشْهَدُهُ is a second naʿt; the hāʾ is a direct object (mafʿūl bihi) and الْمُقَرَّبُونَ is the agent. (إِنَّ الْأَبْرارَ لَفِي نَعِيمٍ عَلَى الْأَرائِكِ يَنْظُرُونَ): a resumptive utterance, introduced to begin on the merits of their conditions; إن and its noun; the shifted lām; فِي نَعِيمٍ is its predicate; عَلَى الْأَرائِكِ is attached to يَنْظُرُونَ, and the clause يَنْظُرُونَ is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in the predicate of إن, or is resumptive. What is meant by الأرائك is the couches in the canopies, and al-ḥijāl, as al-Jawharī says, is the plural of ḥijla (with vowelled letters), whose singular is ḥijāl al-ʿarūs, a chamber adorned with cloths and beds. Al-Shihāb said: al-ḥajla (with two fatḥas) is a square chamber of fine cloths hung over the bed, called in common usage al-nāmūsiyya, i.e. the curtain. (تَعْرِفُ فِي وُجُوهِهِمْ نَضْرَةَ النَّعِيمِ): a resumptive utterance, introduced to notify the one addressed to turn to them and contemplate the traces of bliss on their faces. It was also read in the passive, in which case نَضْرَةَ النَّعِيمِ is the deputy agent; فِي وُجُوهِهِمْ is attached to تَعْرِفُ, and نَضْرَةَ النَّعِيمِ is the direct object. (يُسْقَوْنَ مِنْ رَحِيقٍ مَخْتُومٍ خِتامُهُ مِسْكٌ وَفِي ذلِكَ فَلْيَتَنافَسِ الْمُتَنافِسُونَ): يُسْقَوْنَ is an imperfect passive verb, the wāw is the deputy agent; مِنْ رَحِيقٍ is attached to يُسْقَوْنَ; مَخْتُومٍ is a naʿt, that is, wine pure of every impurity or adulteration; خِتامُهُ مِسْكٌ is a mubtadaʾ and khabar, the clause being a second naʿt of رَحِيقٍ. The apparent sense is that the rahīq is sealed to ensure cleanliness and a musky fragrance, as he explains afterwards. In al-Ṣiḥāḥ: "al-khitām is the clay with which one seals," and Mujāhid and Ibn Zayd said likewise: its vessel is sealed with musk instead of clay. He said:
كأن مشعشعا من خمر بصرى ... نمته البحت مشدود الختام
(As if it were a diluted wine of Buṣrā, pure ones bred it, its seal fastened.)
The wāw is a conjunction; فِي ذلِكَ is attached to the phrase فَلْيَتَنافَسِ; the fāʾ is a conjunction for added emphasis; the lām is the lām of command; يَتَنافَسِ is an imperfect verb jussive by the lām; الْمُتَنافِسُونَ is the agent. In al-Mukhtār: "nafusa al-shayʾ (of the pattern ẓarufa): it became desirable; nāfasa fī al-shayʾ, munāfasatan and nifāsan (with kasra), when he desired it in a spirit of rivalry in generosity; tanāfasū fīhi: they desired it." (وَمِزاجُهُ مِنْ تَسْنِيمٍ عَيْناً يَشْرَبُ بِهَا الْمُقَرَّبُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; مِزاجُهُ is a mubtadaʾ and مِنْ تَسْنِيمٍ its khabar. It is a proper name of a specific spring, named al-tasnīm, which is the maṣdar of sannamahu, "he raised it", because it comes to them from above; as reported, it flows through the air, and they drink it pure, those brought near, and it is mixed for the rest of the people of Paradise. It was also said that it was named al-tasnīm because it is the highest drink in Paradise. عَيْناً is accusative as praise by an omitted verb, its implied form being "I praise"; al-Zajjāj said: it is accusative as a ḥāl from تَسْنِيمٍ since it is described as a proper name. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It was also said that tasnīm is a maṣdar and it is what puts عَيْناً in the accusative." Al-Akhfash said: "they are given to drink a spring."
The clause يَشْرَبُ is a naʿt of عَيْناً, and بِها is attached to يَشْرَبُ, i.e. "from it", on the view that the implication (taḍmīn) lies in the particle; or the implication lies in the verb, i.e. he delights in it; الْمُقَرَّبُونَ is the agent of يَشْرَبُ. (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ أَجْرَمُوا كانُوا مِنَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا يَضْحَكُونَ): a resumptive utterance, introduced to console the believers and strengthen their hearts with what has been prepared for the righteous in Paradise. إن and its noun; the clause أَجْرَمُوا has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of الَّذِينَ; the clause كانُوا is the predicate of إن; كان and its subject; مِنَ الَّذِينَ is attached to يَضْحَكُونَ, and the clause يَضْحَكُونَ is the predicate of كانُوا. The polytheists of Mecca, such as Abū Jahl, al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil and their followers, used to laugh at ʿAmmār, Ṣuhayb, Khabbāb, Bilāl and others of the poor believers and mock them. It was also said that ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, came with a group of believers and the hypocrites mocked them, laughed and winked at one another, then returned to their companions and said, "Today we saw the bald one," and laughed at him. (وَإِذا مَرُّوا بِهِمْ يَتَغامَزُونَ وَإِذَا انْقَلَبُوا إِلى أَهْلِهِمُ انْقَلَبُوا فَكِهِينَ)
The wāw is a conjunction; إذا is a future adverbial containing the sense of a condition, attached to يَتَغامَزُونَ; the clause مَرُّوا بِهِمْ is in the position of a genitive by the annexation of the adverbial to it; the clause يَتَغامَزُونَ has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional. إذا is again a future adverbial; the clause انْقَلَبُوا is in the position of a genitive by the annexation of the adverbial to it; إِلى أَهْلِهِمُ is attached to انْقَلَبُوا; the clause انْقَلَبُوا has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional; فَكِهِينَ is a ḥāl, i.e. delighted with themselves. It was also read فاكِهِينَ, i.e. rejoicing and luxuriating. (وَإِذا رَأَوْهُمْ قالُوا إِنَّ هؤُلاءِ لَضالُّونَ): the wāw is likewise a conjunction; إذا is a future adverbial; the clause رَأَوْهُمْ is in the position of a genitive by the annexation of the adverbial to it; the clause قالُوا has no grammatical position. The nominative pronoun refers to the believers and the accusative to the sinners, i.e. when the believers see the sinners they ascribe error to them; the reverse is permissible. إن with its noun and predicate; the clause is the content of what they said. (وَما أُرْسِلُوا عَلَيْهِمْ حافِظِينَ): the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and the clause is a ḥāl from the wāw in قالُوا; ما is negative; أُرْسِلُوا is a passive past verb, the wāw being the deputy agent; عَلَيْهِمْ is attached to حافِظِينَ, and حافِظِينَ is a ḥāl. (فَالْيَوْمَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنَ الْكُفَّارِ يَضْحَكُونَ عَلَى الْأَرائِكِ يَنْظُرُونَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction of consequence; الْيَوْمَ is an adverbial attached to يَضْحَكُونَ; الَّذِينَ is a mubtadaʾ; the clause آمَنُوا is a ṣila; مِنَ الْكُفَّارِ is likewise attached to يَضْحَكُونَ; the clause يَضْحَكُونَ is the khabar of الَّذِينَ; عَلَى الْأَرائِكِ is attached to يَنْظُرُونَ; the clause يَنْظُرُونَ is a ḥāl from the pronoun in يَضْحَكُونَ, i.e. they laugh while looking at them and at the abasement and humiliation they are in. (هَلْ ثُوِّبَ الْكُفَّارُ ما كانُوا يَفْعَلُونَ): the clause is the content of an omitted saying, i.e. "they say: has it been requited..." They also allowed that the clause be suspended by the interrogative, in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition. ثُوِّبَ is a passive past verb and الْكُفَّارُ is the deputy agent; ثُوِّبَ here means requital, i.e. "have they been rewarded," or it is from thāba meaning "to return," because thawāb is what returns to a person in return for his deed. ما is in the position of an accusative, a second direct object; the clause كانُوا is the ṣila of ما, and the clause يَفْعَلُونَ is the predicate of كانُوا. Aws said:
سأجزيك أو يجزيك عنّي مثوب ... وحسبك أن يثني عليك وتحمدي
(I shall repay you, or one who rewards will repay you on my behalf; and it suffices you that you be praised and commended.)

* Rhetoric:
In the words «كَلَّا إِنَّهُمْ عَنْ رَبِّهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ لَمَحْجُوبُونَ» there is a representation (tamthīl) of the contempt and humiliation shown them, for permission to enter upon people of high rank and lofty station is given only to the honoured ones brought near to them, and only the lowly, marked by baseness, contemptibility and smallness, are barred from them. Abū Tammām gazed at the sky of this meaning when he justified al-Muʿtaṣim's withdrawal from his subjects:
ليس الحجاب بمقص عنك لي أملا ... إن السماء ترجى حين تحتجب
(The veil does not remove from you any hope of mine; the sky is hoped for even when it is veiled.)

farraa:1-1.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيْلٌ لِّلْمُطَفِّفِينَ﴾.
It was revealed at the very beginning of the Prophet's ﷺ arrival in Medina. Its people, when they bought by measure or weight, would take in full and more; and when they sold by measure or weight, they would give short. So ﴿وَيْلٌ لِّلْمُطَفِّفِينَ﴾ was revealed, and they desisted; and they are the fullest of people in measure to this day of theirs.
[He said:] al-Farrāʾ said: It is mentioned that "ويل" is a valley in Hell; and [it is also] the woe that we know.

farraa:2-2.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱكْتَالُواْ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ﴾.
He means: they took measure from the people. The two — على and من — alternate in this place, because it is a right due from him. When he says: اكتلت عليك, it is as though he said: I took what was due from you; and when he says: اكتلت منك, it is likewise: I took in full from you.

farraa:3-3.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَا كَالُوهُمْ أَوْ وَّزَنُوهُمْ﴾.
The hāʾ is in the position of the accusative. You say: قد كِلتك طعاماً كثيراً (I have measured out much food to you), and كِلتني مثله (and you measured the like of it to me), meaning: كِلتَ لي and كِلتُ لك. A Bedouin woman was heard saying: "When the people return [from the watering place], we come to the merchant, and he measures out to us (فيكيلنا) a mudd or two mudds until the next season." This is evidence; and it is of the speech of the people of the Ḥijāz and those of Qays who neighbour them.

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَوْمَ يَقُومُ ٱلنَّاسُ﴾.
It is an explanation of the day in the genitive; since the lām was dropped from the second, he took it back to "مبعوثون، يومَ يقومُ الناس" (resurrected, on the day mankind stands). If you put يوم in the genitive by referring it back to the first اليوم, it would be correct.
It may also be in the position of the genitive, except that it was annexed to يفعل and so took the accusative, since it was annexed to something not purely [nominal]. And if ﴿يَوْمَ يَقُومُ ٱلنَّاسُ﴾ were put in the nominative on that [basis] [Translator's note: the sentence is left incomplete in the source], as the poet said:
فَكُنْتُ كذى رِجْلين: رجلٌ صحيحةٌ * وأخرى رمَى فيها الزَّمانُ فَشَلَّتِ
(And I was like one with two legs: a sound leg, and another at which time took aim, and it was crippled.)

farraa:8-8.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَآ أَدْرَاكَ مَا سِِجِّينٌ﴾.
They mentioned that it is the rock beneath the earth. We consider it to be one of its attributes, because if it were a name for it, it would not be declined as a triptote.
If you said: "I declined it because I took الصخرة (the rock) to mean the stone (الحجر) in which the record is", that would be a valid interpretation.

farraa:14-14.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَلاَّ بَلْ رَانَ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمْ مَّا كَانُواْ يَكْسِبُونَ﴾.
He says: acts of disobedience and sins multiplied in them and encompassed their hearts; that is the rust (الرين) on them. It has come in the hadith that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah have mercy on him, said of al-Usayfiʿ: "He has become one overwhelmed (رِين به)." He means: debt has encompassed his wealth [131/b]. One of the Arabs recited to me:
* لم ترو حتى هجرت ورين بى *
(She had not quenched her thirst until midday came, and I was overcome.)
He says: until I was overcome by exhaustion; likewise the overwhelming of debt and the overwhelming of sins.

farraa:18-18.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَلاَّ إِنَّ كِتَابَ ٱلأَبْرَارِ لَفِي عِلِّيِّينَ﴾.
Someone may say: How was (عِلِّيّون) pluralised with nūn, when this is [a form] of the plural of men? [The answer is] that when the Arabs form a plural for which they do not consider there to be a structure of a singular and a dual, they say it with nūn for the feminine and the masculine. Of that kind is this; it is one thing above another, whose singular and dual are not known.
I heard one of the Arabs say: أطعمنا مرقةَ مرقَين (he fed us broth of two broths), meaning: meats when they are cooked in broth.
He said: al-Farrāʾ said another time: cooked in one water. The poet said:
قد رَوِيَتْ إلا الدُّهَيْدِهينَا * قُلَيِّصاتٍ وأُبَيْكِرينَا
(They have quenched their thirst, except the little herd — little young she-camels and little young he-camels.)
He pluralised with nūn because he meant a number that is not limited. Likewise the saying of the poet:
فأصبحت المذَاهِبُ قد أذاعت * بِهَا الإعصارُ بعد الوابلينا
(And the paths had become such that the whirlwinds had scattered them, after the heavy rains.)
He meant: rain after rain, without limit. We consider that the Arabs' saying عشرون and ثلاثون — since it is used for women and men — is of the [kind of] number that resembles this type. Likewise عليّون: elevation after elevation, as though it had no end.

farraa:24-24.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تَعْرِفُ فِي وُجُوهِهِمْ نَضْرَةَ ٱلنَّعِيمِ﴾.
He says: the glow of bliss and its moistness [«ونداء» in the source — Translator's note: apparently for «ونداه»]. The readers agree on (تعرف) except Abū Jaʿfar al-Madanī, who read: "تُعرَفُ فى وجُوهِهِمْ نَضْرَةُ النَّعِيم"; "يُعرف" is also permissible, because النضرة is a feminine noun derived from a verb, and making its verb before it masculine [132/a] or feminine are both permissible,
like His saying [«قوه» in the source]: ﴿وأَخَذَ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا الصَّيْحَةُ﴾, and in another place: ﴿وأخذَت﴾.

farraa:26-26.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿خَاتَمُهُ مِسْكٌ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan, the people of the Ḥijāz, ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash read "ختامه مسك". Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: [and] Muḥammad ibn al-Faḍl narrated to me from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān from ʿAlī that he read "خَاتَمُهُ مِسْكٌ". [Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us], saying: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: [and] Abū al-Aḥwaṣ narrated to me from Ashʿath ibn Abī al-Shaʿthāʾ al-Muḥāribī [«الشعناء» in the source], who said: ʿAlqama ibn Qays read "خاتَمُهُ مِسْكٌ", and said: Have you not seen the woman say to the perfumer: "Make its end (خاتمه) musk for me", meaning its last part? الخاتم and الختام are close in meaning, except that الخاتم is the noun and الختام is the maṣdar (verbal noun). Al-Farazdaq said:
فَبِتْنَ جنابَتىَّ مُصَرَّعَاتٍ * وبِتُّ أفُضُّ أَغْلاَقَ الخِتامِ
(They spent the night at my two sides, laid low, and I spent the night breaking the locks of the seal.)
Similar to الخاتم and الختام is your saying of a man: هو كريم الطابع and الطباع (he is of noble character). Its interpretation: when one of them drinks, he finds at the end of his cup the scent of musk.

farraa:27-27.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِزَاجُهُ﴾.
The mixture of the sealed wine (الرحيق) is ﴿مِن تَسْنِيمٍ﴾: from water that comes down upon them from heights. He said: ﴿من تسنيم، عيناً﴾ — a spring that comes down upon them from above. (عيناً) is accusative on two grounds. One of them: that you intend من تسنيمِ عينٍ (from the pouring down of a spring); when you add tanwīn, you put [what follows] in the accusative,
as whoever read it read: ﴿أَوْ إِطْعَامٌ فِى يَوْمٍ ذِى مَسْغَبَةٍ، يتيماً﴾, and as He said: ﴿أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ الأَرْضَ كِفَاتاً، أَحْيَاءً وَأَمْوَاتاً﴾, and as whoever said it said: ﴿فَجَزَاءٌ مِثْلَ ما قَتلَ مِنَ النِّعمِ﴾. The other ground: that you intend: from water poured down from above as a spring (سُنِّم عيناً).
as in your saying: رفع عيناً يشرب بها (He raised a spring from which one drinks). If التسنيم is [not] a name for the water, then العين is indefinite and التسنيم definite; and if it is a name for the water, then العين is definite [Translator's note: so in the source; the logic suggests the two clauses may be reversed], so it also comes out in the accusative.

farraa:31-31.t: His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَاكِهِينَ﴾: delighted. It has also been read: "فَكِهين", and both are correct, like طمِع and طامع.

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: «ويل»: mubtadaʾ (subject); «للمطففين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate); beginning with an indefinite noun is permitted because it indicates an imprecation (duʿāʾ).

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: «الذين» is a naʿt (adjective) of {لِلْمُطَفِّفِينَ}, and the conditional clause is the ṣila (relative clause); one says: اكتَلْتُ على الناس and اكتَلْتُ منهم (I took measure from the people).

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: «أنَّ» and what follows it stand in place of the two objects of «يظن».

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: «يوم»: an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) an implied verb, i.e.: they will be raised on the day; the preposition «لرب» is attached to «يقوم».

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: (كلا إن كتاب الفجار لفي سجين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The wāw is resumptive; «ما» is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); and the clause «ما سجِّين» is the second object of «أدراك».

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: His saying «كتاب»: khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: it is a book; and the clause is explicative of {سِجِّينٌ}.

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: (وما يكذب به إلا كل معتد أثيم) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive; «كل»: fāʿil (agent); and «إلا» is for restriction (ḥaṣr).

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: (إذا تتلى عليه آياتنا قال أساطير الأولين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The conditional clause is a second naʿt (adjective) of {مُعْتَدٍ}.

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: The clause «ران» is resumptive; «ما»: a relative noun, the fāʿil (agent) of «ران».

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: The preposition «عن ربهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «محجوبون», and so is the adverb.

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: (ثم إنهم لصالو الجحيم) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is conjoined to the clause «إنهم لمحجوبون».

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: The clause «يقال» is conjoined to the clause {إِنَّهُمْ لَصَالُو}.

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: The clause «ما عِليُّون» is the second object of «أدراك», and the clause «وما أدراك» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: «كتاب»: khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: it is a book; and the clause is explicative of {عِلِّيُّونَ}.

harrat-mujtaba:21-21.t: The clause «يشهده المقربون» is a second naʿt (adjective).

harrat-mujtaba:23-23.t: The clause «ينظرون» is a second khabar (predicate) of {إِنَّ}; the preposition «على الأرائك» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ينظرون».

harrat-mujtaba:24-24.t: The clause «تعرف» is a third khabar (predicate) of {إِنَّ}.

harrat-mujtaba:25-25.t: The clause «يُسْقَون» is a fourth khabar (predicate) of {إِنَّ}

harrat-mujtaba:26-26.t: The clause «ختامه مسك» is a second naʿt (adjective) of {رَحِيقٍ}; the preposition «في ذلك» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb «يتنافس», and the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida); and the clause «يتنافس» is parenthetical between the two conjoined items.

harrat-mujtaba:27-27.t: The clause «ومزاجه من تسنيم» is conjoined to the clause {خِتَامُهُ مِسْكٌ}.

harrat-mujtaba:28-28.t: «عينًا»: object of an implied (أعني) (I mean); and the clause «يشرب» is a naʿt (adjective).

harrat-mujtaba:29-29.t: The preposition «من الذين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يضحكون»

harrat-mujtaba:30-30.t: (وإذا مروا بهم يتغامزون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The conditional clause is conjoined to the ṣila (relative clause) {يَضْحَكُونَ}.

harrat-mujtaba:31-31.t: «فكهين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw.

harrat-mujtaba:33-33.t: The clause «وما أرسلوا» is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); «حافظين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw in «أرسلوا»

harrat-mujtaba:34-34.t: The fāʾ is resumptive; «اليوم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يضحكون»; the clause «يضحكون» is the khabar (predicate) of «الذين»; the preposition «من الكفار» is attached to «يضحكون».

harrat-mujtaba:35-35.t: The clause «ينظرون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of {يَضْحَكُونَ}.

harrat-mujtaba:36-36.t: «ما»: a relative noun, second object; and the clause «هل ثُوِّب» is resumptive.

mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, the Exalted: (ويل للمطففين): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). The preferred choice for (ويل) and the like, when it is not annexed, is the nominative, and the accusative is permissible; if it is annexed or made definite, the preferred choice in it is the accusative, as in His saying (ويلكم لا تفتروا). (ويل) is in origin a maṣdar (verbal noun) of a verb that is not used. Al-Mubarrad said of (ويل للمطففين), (ويل يومئذ للمكذبين) and the like: only the nominative is permissible in it, because it is not an imprecation against them; it is only a report that this is established for them. If the maṣdar is of a used verb, the preferred choice in it, when it is annexed or made definite with alif and lām, is the nominative, and the accusative is permissible; if it is indefinite, the preferred choice is the accusative and the nominative is permissible: as in (الحمد لله) and (الشكر لزيد), where the nominative is the preferred choice, and (حمدا لله) and (شكرا له), where the accusative is the preferred choice when it is indefinite, the opposite of the first. All of that has been mentioned [before].

mekki-muskil:3-3.t:
His saying (كالوهم أو وزنوهم): (هم) may be a nominative pronoun emphasising the wāw in (كالوا) and (وزنوا), in which case it would be written with an alif; or it may be an object pronoun in the position of the accusative governed by (كالوا) or (وزنوا), in which case it is written without an alif after the wāw; and in the Muṣḥaf it is without an alif.
(على) in His saying (على الناس) is in the place of (من). (كال) and (وزن) take two objects, one by a preposition and the other without a preposition.

mekki-muskil:6-6.t: His saying (يوم يقوم الناس): (يوم) is accusative as an adverbial, and its governor is a verb indicated by (مبعوثون), i.e. "they will be resurrected on the day mankind stands". It may also be a badal (substitute) from (ليوم) according to its position. It is indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa according to the Kufans, its position being accusative as we mentioned, and declinable, accusative, according to the Basrans.

mekki-muskil:7-7.t: His saying (سجين): it is on the pattern fiʿʿīl from (السجل) "register", the nūn replacing the lām. It is also said that it is fiʿʿīl from (السجن) "prison".

mekki-muskil:8-8.t: His saying (وما أدراك ما سجين): the discussion of it and of its parallel has already preceded in al-Ḥāqqa and elsewhere.

mekki-muskil:9-9.t:
His saying (كتاب): nominative as the khabar (predicate) of (إن), the adverbial phrase being inoperative (mulghā); or it is a khabar after a khabar; or with an implied (هو).
His saying (ثم يقال هذا الذي): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar, in the position of the object whose agent is not named [nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)], according to Sībawayh. Al-Mubarrad said: the maṣdar (verbal noun) is implied and stands in the place of the agent; according to him a clause cannot stand in the place of the agent.

mekki-muskil:13-13.t: His saying (قال أساطير): nominative with an implied (هذه) "these are".

mekki-muskil:18-18.t: His saying (لفي عليين): it is a plural with no singular from its own word, like (عشرين) "twenty", so it is treated like it. It has also been said that (عليين) is an adjective of the angels, which is why it is pluralised with wāw and nūn.

mekki-muskil:27-28.t:
His saying (من تسنيم عينا): (عين) is accusative according to al-Akhfash by (يسقون); according to al-Mubarrad with an implied "I mean" (أعني); and according to al-Farrāʾ by (تسنيم): it should properly, in his view, have been annexed, but when (تسنيما) was given nunation, (عينا) was made accusative by it. It is also said that it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), in the sense of "flowing", so it is a ḥāl from (تسنيم), on the basis that (تسنيم) is a name for water flowing from on high, as if it flows from the heights of Paradise; so it is definite, its implied form being "and its mixture is of the lofty water, flowing from on high".
His saying (يشرب بها): a naʿt (adjective) of (العين), and (بها) means "from it" (منها).

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿ويل﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿للمطففين﴾: the lām is a preposition and al-muṭaffifīn is a noun in the genitive by the preposition ﴿اللام﴾, the sign of its genitive being the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of ﴿ويل﴾. The clause ﴿ويل للمطففين﴾ is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿الذين﴾: a relative noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿المطففين﴾.
﴿إذا﴾: an adverb indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an implied ﴿قبضوا﴾ or ﴿استوفوا﴾.
﴿اكتالوا﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent).
﴿على﴾: a preposition.
﴿الناس﴾: a noun in the genitive by ﴿على﴾, the sign of its genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿اكتالوا﴾.
﴿يستوفون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs; the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil. The clause ﴿كالوهم﴾ [Translator's note: so in the source; the clause in this ayah is ﴿اكتالوا﴾, and ﴿كالوهم﴾ belongs to the next ayah] is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt of ﴿المطففين﴾; the clause ﴿يستوفون﴾ is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition, or it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the implied apodosis, i.e. "qabaḍū mustawfīn" (they took receipt, taking in full).

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿وإذا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and idhā is an adverb for future time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted apodosis (jawāb), its implied form being "istawfaw lahā" (they took it in full).
﴿كالوهم﴾: a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma; the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent), and hum is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿أو﴾: a conjunction.
﴿وزنوهم﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the ḍamma; the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil, and hum is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi.
﴿يخسرون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs; the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil. The clause ﴿كالوهم﴾ is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it; the clause ﴿وزنوهم﴾ is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to ﴿كالوهم﴾; and the clause ﴿يخسرون﴾ is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition, with no grammatical position, or it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the implied apodosis, i.e. "qabaḍū mustawfīn" (they took receipt, taking in full). [Translator's note: the implied forms "istawfaw lahā" and "qabaḍū mustawfīn" in this entry repeat the wording of the previous ayah, which concerns taking in full, whereas this ayah concerns giving short measure; translated as written.]

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿ألا﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval (istifhām inkārī), and lā is a negative particle indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn.
﴿يظن﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma.
﴿أولئك﴾: a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent); the kāf is for address.
﴿أنهم﴾: anna is a maṣdar-forming and accusative particle indeclinable on the fatḥa, and the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of the accusative as the noun (ism) of anna. The interpreted maṣdar from ﴿أنهم مبعوثون﴾ stands in place of the two objects of yaẓunnu.
﴿مبعوثون﴾: khabar (predicate) of anna, nominative by the ḍamma. The clause ﴿ألا يظن﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿ليوم﴾: the lām is a preposition, and yawm is a genitive noun by the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿مبعوثون﴾.
﴿عظيم﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿يوم﴾, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the kasra.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿يوم﴾: an adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, i.e. "yubʿathūn" (they are resurrected).
﴿يقوم﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma.
﴿الناس﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative by the ḍamma.
﴿لرب﴾: the lām is a preposition, and the word ﴿رب﴾ is a noun in the genitive by the lām, the sign of the genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿يقوم﴾.
﴿العالمين﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive by the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural. The clause ﴿يقوم﴾ is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿كلا﴾: a particle of deterrence and rebuke.
﴿إن﴾: a particle of emphasis and accusative, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa.
﴿كتاب﴾: the noun (ism) of inna, accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa.
﴿الفجار﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive by the kasra.
﴿لفي﴾: the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and fī is a preposition.
﴿سجين﴾: a noun in the genitive by the preposition, the sign of its genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of inna. The clause ﴿إن كتاب الفجار لفي سجين﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿وما﴾: the wāw is parenthetical, and mā is an interrogative noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿أدراك﴾: a past verb indeclinable on an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the alif; the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa", and the kāf is a pronoun indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿ما﴾: an interrogative noun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ.
﴿سجين﴾: khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma. The clause ﴿ما سجين﴾ is in the position of the accusative, standing in place of the second and third objects of the verb ﴿أدراك﴾, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative; the clause ﴿أدراك...﴾ is in the position of the nominative as khabar of the first mubtadaʾ ﴿ما﴾; and the clause ﴿وما أدراك ما سجين﴾ is parenthetical, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿كتاب﴾: khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "huwa".
﴿مرقوم﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿كتاب﴾, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma. The clause ﴿هو كتاب﴾ is resumptive by way of explanation (istiʾnāf bayānī), with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿ويل﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma.
﴿يومئذ﴾: yawm: an adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa, a badal (substitute) from yawm in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿يوم يقوم الناس لرب العالمين﴾; idh: a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied (muqaddar) sukūn, because the place is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation, in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the tanwīn compensates for an omitted clause, the implied form being "yawma idh yaqūmu al-nāsu li-rabbi al-ʿālamīn" (the day when mankind stand before the Lord of the worlds).
﴿للمكذبين﴾: the lām is a preposition and al-mukadhdhibīn is a genitive noun, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural. The clause ﴿ويل يومئذ للمكذبين﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t:
﴿الذين﴾: a relative noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿المكذبين﴾.
﴿يكذبون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs; the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent).
﴿بيوم﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition and yawm is a genitive noun, the sign of the genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يكذبون﴾.
﴿الدين﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive by the kasra. The clause ﴿يكذبون﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿وما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction or circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and mā is a negative particle indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn.
﴿يكذب﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma.
﴿به﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition and the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the kasra in the position of the genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يكذبون﴾ [Translator's note: so in the source; the verb in this ayah is ﴿يكذب﴾].
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr), indeclinable on the sukūn.
﴿كل﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative by the ḍamma.
﴿معتد﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive by an implied (muqaddar) kasra on the yāʾ, which is dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.
﴿أثيم﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿معتد﴾, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the kasra. The clause ﴿ما يكذب...﴾ is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of yawm al-dīn, or it is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:13-13.t:
﴿إذا﴾: an adverb of the future containing the sense of condition, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿قال﴾.
﴿تتلى﴾: a passive imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the alif, owing to impossibility (taʿadhdhur).
﴿عليه﴾: ʿalā is a preposition and the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable (mabnī) on the kasra in the position of the genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿تتلى﴾.
﴿آياتنا﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative by the ḍamma, and nā is an indeclinable pronoun in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿قال﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being ﴿هو﴾.
﴿أساطير﴾: khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being ﴿هذا﴾, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿الأولين﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural. The clause ﴿إذا تتلى عليه آياتنا قال﴾ is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿كل﴾ muʿtad; the clause ﴿تتلى﴾ is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the clause ﴿قال﴾ is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition, with no grammatical position; and the clause ﴿هذا أساطير الأولين﴾ is in the position of the accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).

muyesser-irab:14-14.t:
﴿كلا﴾: a particle of deterrence and rebuke.
﴿بل﴾: a particle of conjunction and digression (iḍrāb).
﴿ران﴾: a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa.
﴿على قلوبهم﴾: ʿalā is a preposition, qulūb is a genitive noun, and hum is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ران﴾.
﴿ما﴾: a relative noun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent).
﴿كانوا﴾: kāna is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as the noun (ism) of kāna.
﴿يكسبون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs; the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil. The clause ﴿ران﴾ has no grammatical position because it is resumptive; ﴿كانوا﴾ has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾; and the clause yaksibūn is in the position of the accusative as khabar (predicate) of kānū.

muyesser-irab:15-15.t:
﴿كلا﴾: a particle of deterrence and rebuke.
﴿إنهم﴾: inna is a particle of emphasis and accusative indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and hum is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the accusative as the noun (ism) of inna.
﴿عن﴾: a preposition.
﴿ربهم﴾: a genitive noun, and hum is an indeclinable pronoun in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿محجوبون﴾.
﴿يومئذ﴾: yawm: an adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa, attached to ﴿محجوبون﴾; idh: a noun indeclinable on an implied (muqaddar) sukūn, because the place is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation, in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the tanwīn compensates for an omitted clause, the implied form being "yawma idh yaqūmu al-nāsu li-rabbi al-ʿālamīn" (the day when mankind stand before the Lord of the worlds). [Translator's note: this implied form repeats the one given for 83:10; translated as written.]
﴿لمحجوبون﴾: the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) for emphasis, and maḥjūbūn is khabar (predicate) of inna, nominative (marfūʿ) by the wāw because it is a sound masculine plural. The clause ﴿إنهم عن ربهم لمحجوبون﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:16-16.t:
﴿ثم﴾: a conjunction for distance in rank.
﴿إنهم﴾: inna is a particle of emphasis and accusative indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and hum is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the accusative as the noun (ism) of inna.
﴿لصالو﴾: the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and ṣālū is khabar (predicate) of inna, nominative (marfūʿ) by the wāw because it is a sound masculine plural; the nūn was dropped because of the annexation (iḍāfa).
﴿الجحيم﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive, the sign of its genitive being the kasra. The clause ﴿إنهم لصالو الجحيم﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿إنهم عن ربهم يومئذ لمحجوبون﴾, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:17-17.t:
﴿ثم﴾: a conjunction for sequence with delay.
﴿يقال﴾: a passive imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "huwa".
﴿هذا﴾: a demonstrative indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿الذي﴾: a relative noun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as khabar (predicate) of ﴿هذا﴾.
﴿كنتم﴾: kun [Translator's note: so in the source, i.e. the stem of kāna as it appears in kuntum] is a past verb indeclinable on the sukūn, and tum is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as the noun (ism) of kun.
﴿به﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition and the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the kasra in the position of the genitive.
﴿تكذبون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs; the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent). The clause ﴿يقال هذا الذي كنتم به تكذبون﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿إنهم لصالو الجحيم﴾, with no grammatical position; the clause ﴿كنتم﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; and ﴿تكذبون﴾ is in the position of the accusative as khabar of kuntum.

muyesser-irab:18-18.t:
﴿كلا﴾: a particle of emphasis and deterrence.
﴿إن﴾: a particle of emphasis and accusative, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa.
﴿كتاب﴾: the noun (ism) of inna, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.
﴿الأبرار﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive by the kasra.
﴿لفي﴾: the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and fī is a preposition.
