﴿عليين﴾: a noun in the genitive by the preposition, the sign of its genitive being the yāʾ because it is treated like (mulḥaq bi-) the sound masculine plural; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of inna. The clause ﴿إن كتاب الفجار لفي عليين﴾ [Translator's note: so in the source; the ayah reads ﴿إن كتاب الأبرار لفي عليين﴾] is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:19-19.t:
﴿وما﴾: the wāw is parenthetical, and mā is an interrogative noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿أدراك﴾: a past verb indeclinable on an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the alif; the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa", and the kāf is a pronoun indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿ما﴾: an interrogative noun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ.
﴿عليون﴾: khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the wāw because it is treated like (mulḥaq bi-) the sound masculine plural. The clause ﴿ما عليون﴾ is in the position of the accusative, standing in place of the second and third objects of the verb ﴿أدراك﴾, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative; the clause ﴿أدراك﴾ is in the position of the nominative as khabar of the first mubtadaʾ ﴿ما﴾; and the clause ﴿وما أدراك ما عليون﴾ is parenthetical, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:20-20.t:
﴿كتاب﴾: khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being ﴿هو﴾.
﴿مرقوم﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿كتاب﴾, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma. The clause ﴿هو كتاب﴾ is resumptive by way of explanation (istiʾnāf bayānī), with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:21-21.t:
﴿يشهده﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma, and the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿المقربون﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative by the wāw because it is a sound masculine plural. The clause ﴿يشهده المقربون﴾ is in the position of the nominative as a second khabar (predicate) of the implied mubtadaʾ (subject) ﴿هو﴾.

muyesser-irab:22-22.t:
﴿إن﴾: a particle of emphasis and accusative, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa.
﴿الأبرار﴾: the noun (ism) of inna, accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa.
﴿لفي﴾: the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and fī is a preposition.
﴿نعيم﴾: a noun in the genitive by the preposition, the sign of its genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of inna. The clause ﴿إن الأبرار...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:23-23.t:
﴿على﴾: a preposition.
﴿الأرائك﴾: a genitive noun, the sign of its genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of yanẓurūn.
﴿ينظرون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs; the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil. The clause ﴿ينظرون﴾ is in the position of the nominative as a second khabar (predicate) of ﴿إن﴾.

muyesser-irab:24-24.t:
﴿تعرف﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being ﴿أنت﴾.
﴿في﴾: a preposition.
﴿وجوههم﴾: wujūh is a genitive noun, the sign of the genitive being the kasra, and hum is a pronoun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تعرف﴾.
﴿نضرة﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa.
﴿النعيم﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive by the kasra. The clause ﴿تعرف﴾ is in the position of the nominative as a third khabar (predicate) of ﴿إن﴾.

muyesser-irab:25-25.t:
﴿يسقون﴾: a passive imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
﴿من﴾: a preposition.
﴿رحيق﴾: a genitive noun by the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يسقون﴾.
﴿مختوم﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿رحيق﴾, genitive by the kasra. The clause ﴿يسقون﴾ is in the position of the nominative as a fourth khabar (predicate) of ﴿إن﴾.

muyesser-irab:26-26.t:
﴿ختامه﴾: khitām is mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma, and the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿مسك﴾: khabar (predicate), nominative by the ḍamma. The clause ﴿ختامه مسك﴾ is in the position of the genitive as a second naʿt (adjective) of ﴿رحيق﴾.
﴿و﴾: the wāw is parenthetical.
﴿في﴾: a preposition.
﴿ذلك﴾: a demonstrative indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of the genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يتنافس﴾.
﴿فليتنافس﴾: the fāʾ: occurring in the apodosis of an implied condition; the lām is the lām of command, and yatanāfas is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lām, the sign of its jussive being the sukūn.
﴿المتنافسون﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative by the wāw because it is a sound masculine plural. The clause ﴿فليتنافس...﴾ is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the implied condition, i.e. "if competition is to take place, then let them compete…". The implied conditional sentence is parenthetical, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:27-27.t:
﴿ومزاجه﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and mizāj is mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma, and the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿من﴾: a preposition.
﴿تسنيم﴾: a genitive noun, the sign of its genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of ﴿مزاجه﴾. The clause ﴿مزاجه من تسنيم﴾ is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause ﴿ختامه مسك﴾.

muyesser-irab:28-28.t:
﴿عينا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), of an omitted verb whose implied form is "aʿnī" (I mean) or "amdaḥu" (I praise); the sign of the accusative is the fatḥa.
﴿يشرب﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma.
﴿بها﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition, and ﴿ها﴾ is an indeclinable pronoun in the position of the genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يشرب﴾.
﴿المقربون﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative by the wāw because it is a sound masculine plural. The clause ﴿يشرب﴾ is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿عينًا﴾.

muyesser-irab:29-29.t:
﴿إن﴾: a particle of emphasis and accusative, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa.
﴿الذين﴾: a relative noun indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative as the noun (ism) of inna.
﴿أجرموا﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent).
﴿كانوا﴾: kāna is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as the noun (ism) of kāna.
﴿من﴾: a preposition.
﴿الذين﴾: a relative noun indeclinable on the fatḥa in the position of the genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يضحكون﴾.
﴿آمنوا﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil.
﴿يضحكون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs; the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil. The clause ﴿إن الذين أجرموا كانوا﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position; the clause ﴿أجرموا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of alladhīna, with no grammatical position; the clause ﴿كانوا﴾ is in the position of the nominative as khabar (predicate) of inna; the clause ﴿آمنوا﴾ is the ṣila of the second relative noun, with no grammatical position; and the clause ﴿يضحكون﴾ is in the position of the accusative as khabar of ﴿كانوا﴾.

muyesser-irab:30-30.t:
﴿وإذا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and idhā is an adverb of the future indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يتغامزون﴾.
﴿مروا﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent).
﴿بهم﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition and hum is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of the genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿مروا﴾.
﴿يتغامزون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs; the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil. The clause ﴿مروا بهم﴾ is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it, and the clause ﴿يتغامزون﴾ has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.

muyesser-irab:31-31.t:
﴿وإذا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and idhā is an adverb of the future indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿انقلبوا﴾.
﴿انقلبوا﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent).
﴿إلى﴾: a preposition.
﴿أهلهم﴾: a genitive noun, the sign of its genitive being the kasra, and hum is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of the genitive.
﴿انقلبوا﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil.
﴿فاكهين﴾: a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of ﴿انقلبوا﴾, accusative (manṣūb) by the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural. The clause ﴿انقلبوا﴾ is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it, and the clause ﴿انقلبوا﴾ has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.

muyesser-irab:32-32.t:
﴿وإذا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and idhā is an adverb of the future indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿قالوا﴾.
﴿رأوهم﴾: raʾā is a past verb indeclinable on an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the alif, which is dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent), and hum is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿قالوا﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil.
﴿إن﴾: a particle of emphasis and accusative, indeclinable on the fatḥa.
﴿هؤلاء﴾: a demonstrative indeclinable on the kasra, in the position of the accusative as the noun (ism) of inna.
﴿لضالون﴾: the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and ḍāllūn is khabar (predicate) of inna, nominative (marfūʿ) by the wāw because it is a sound masculine plural. The clause ﴿رأوهم﴾ is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it; the clause ﴿قالوا﴾ is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition, with no grammatical position; and the clause ﴿إن هؤلاء لضالون﴾ is in the position of the accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).

muyesser-irab:33-33.t:
﴿وما﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and mā is a negative particle indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn.
﴿أرسلوا﴾: a passive past verb indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
﴿عليهم﴾: ʿalā is a preposition and hum is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of the genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿حافظين﴾.
﴿حافظين﴾: a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun of ﴿أرسلوا﴾, accusative (manṣūb) by the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural. The clause ﴿ما أرسلوا﴾ is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl of the fāʿil (agent) of qālū.

muyesser-irab:34-34.t:
﴿فاليوم﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (signalling an implied condition), and al-yawm is an adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يضحكون﴾.
﴿الذين﴾: a relative noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿آمنوا﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent).
﴿من﴾: a preposition.
﴿الكفار﴾: a genitive noun, the sign of its genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿يضحكون﴾.
﴿يضحكون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs; the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil. The clause ﴿الذين آمنوا من الكفار يضحكون﴾ is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition; the clause ﴿آمنوا﴾ has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun ﴿الذين﴾; and the clause ﴿يضحكون﴾ is in the position of the nominative as khabar (predicate) of ﴿الذين﴾.

muyesser-irab:35-35.t:
﴿على﴾: a preposition.
﴿الأرائك﴾: a genitive noun, the sign of its genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ينظرون﴾.
﴿ينظرون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs; the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent). The clause ﴿ينظرون﴾ is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in ﴿يضحكون﴾.

muyesser-irab:36-36.t:
﴿هل﴾: an interrogative particle indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn.
﴿ثوب﴾: a passive past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa.
﴿الكفار﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma.
﴿ما﴾: a relative noun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the accusative as second mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿كانوا﴾: kāna is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as the noun (ism) of ﴿كان﴾.
﴿يفعلون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs; the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent). The clause ﴿ثُوِّب﴾ is in the position of the accusative as the object of an implied "yaqūlūn" (they say); the clause ﴿كانوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position; and the clause ﴿يفعلون﴾ is in the position of the accusative as khabar (predicate) of ﴿كانوا﴾.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t:
ويلا is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «للمطففين» is its khabar (predicate), i.e. a reproach. The accusative is permissible outside the Qur'an, because ويل has the sense of a maṣdar (verbal noun); the nominative is preferred because no verb from it is uttered, except something irregular (shādhdh) that Muḥammad ibn al-Walīd recited, namely: [al-hazaj] 547-
فما وال ولا واح ... ولا واس أبو هند
(Abū Hind is not one who says "woe", nor "alas", nor "pity".)
If it is derived from a verb, the accusative is preferred according to the grammarians, as in بؤسا له ("misery to him"). If you do not bring the khabar with the first [i.e. with the lām], you use the accusative and say: ويله and ويحه.

nahhas-irab:10-11.t: [الَّذِينَ is] a naʿt (adjective) of المكذبين; the accusative is also permissible, as explained before.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Wāqid said: i.e. a transgressor in his speech, a sinner in the sight of his Lord. [Translator's note: the source names him «الحسن بن واقد»; the known transmitter is al-Ḥusayn ibn Wāqid.]

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: إِذا تُتْلى عَلَيْهِ آياتُنا قالَ أَساطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ (13): [أساطير is nominative] by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject).

nahhas-irab:14-14.t: [بَلْ رانَ] with assimilation (idghām) of the lām into the rāʾ and without inclination (imāla) is the reading of Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr. Al-Aʿmash, ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read with assimilation, except that they used imāla. Al-Ḥasan and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read بَلْ رانَ without assimilation. Abū Jaʿfar said: Assimilation here is preferable because of the closeness of the lām to the rāʾ, and leaving out imāla is preferable because there is no yāʾ or kasra in it; the imāla is only based on the meaning, since it is from ران يرين, derived from الرّين, as was read [in transmission] to Ibrāhīm ibn Mūsā, from Ismāʿīl, from ʿĀrim, who said: I asked al-Aṣmaʿī about the ḥadīth of the Prophet ﷺ «إنه ليغان على قلبي حتى أستغفر الله عزّ وجلّ مائة مرة» ("My heart is clouded over until I ask forgiveness of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, a hundred times"), and he said: Caution in speaking about the ḥadīth of the Messenger of Allah is like caution about the Qur'an; but the Arabs call a cloud, when it is thin, less than a [full] cloud, الغين and الرّين. Abū Jaʿfar said: This is the i'rab and the derivation. As for the meaning, Mujāhid said about it: The heart has fingers; when a servant sins, one finger of it closes, then if he sins another closes, until all of them close and his heart is sealed, so that no admonition benefits it. Abū Jaʿfar said: The best that has been said about this is what is soundly established from the Prophet ﷺ, as was read [in transmission] to Aḥmad ibn Shuʿayb, from Qutayba, from al-Layth, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAjlān, from al-Qaʿqāʿ, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Abū Hurayra, from the Prophet, who said: «When the servant commits a sin, a spot is made on his heart — meaning a black one. If he desists, asks forgiveness and repents, his heart is polished; and if he goes back, it is increased until it covers his heart. That is the rust (الرين) that Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, mentioned: كَلَّا بَلْ رانَ عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ ما كانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ (14).»

nahhas-irab:15-15.t: There are two views on its meaning. One of them is that by this He indicated that the believers will not be veiled from looking at Him, Majestic and Mighty is He. Abū Jaʿfar said: We have mentioned what Mālik ibn Anas said about that. Al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah have mercy on him, was asked about seeing Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, on the Day of Resurrection, and he said: It is indicated by كَلَّا إِنَّهُمْ عَنْ رَبِّهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ لَمَحْجُوبُونَ (15). The other view is that the implied form is "from the honour of their Lord", like وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ [Yūsuf: 82]. Abū Jaʿfar said: This is wrong according to the school of the grammarians, among them al-Khalīl and Sībawayh; according to them, and according to the other grammarians, it is not permissible to say جاءني زيد ("Zayd came to me") meaning "his servant came to me" or "his honour came to me".

nahhas-irab:16-16.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُمْ لَصالُوا الْجَحِيمِ: [the nūn may be dropped or kept] because it refers to the future. Whoever drops the nūn for lightness says لصالو الجحيمِ in the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); whoever drops it because of the meeting of two vowelless letters puts [الجحيمَ] in the accusative.

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: [ثُمَّ يُقالُ هذَا الَّذِي كُنْتُمْ بِهِ تُكَذِّبُونَ: the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)] of the passive verb, according to Sībawayh, is the clause. He said likewise about ثُمَّ بَدا لَهُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ ما رَأَوُا الْآياتِ لَيَسْجُنُنَّهُ [Yūsuf: 35], [that the clause is] in the position of the fāʿil (agent). This, according to Abū al-ʿAbbās, is a mistake, because a clause does not stand in the place of the agent; rather the verb indicates the maṣdar, and the maṣdar stands in the place of the agent.

nahhas-irab:18-19.t: وَما أَدْراكَ ما عِلِّيُّونَ (19): there are five views about it [i.e. its meaning], and two views about its i'rab. Most of the exegetes, among them Kaʿb, Mujāhid and Zayd ibn Aslam, say: علّيّون is the seventh heaven. Al-Farrāʾ reported that it is the lowest heaven. Qatāda said: [it is] the right leg of the Throne. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: علّيّون is the Lote-Tree of the Utmost Boundary. It was also said: علّيّون are the angels. Abū Jaʿfar said: The majority hold the first view. As for the i'rab, the two views about it are: one of them is that عليين resembles عشرين and the like, because it has no singular; it only means "from height to height", so it was declined like عشرين. Abū Jaʿfar said: This view agrees with the interpretation of those who said علّيّون is the seventh heaven. The other view is that عليين is an adjective of the angels, which is why it was given the sound plural with wāw and nūn.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: الَّذِينَ is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of المطففين, or in the accusative as censure (ʿalā al-dhamm); the latter is more fitting for the verse. One who is weak in Arabic may imagine that the meaning of اكتلت عليه and اكتلت منه is the same, but their implied senses differ: the meaning of اكتلت عليه is "I took by measure what was due from him", and the meaning of اكتلت منه is "I took my full due from him".

nahhas-irab:20-20.t: That is, that record is a book (كتاب), i.e. something written. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk explained that, saying: When the spirit of the believer comes out, the angel takes it and ascends with it to the lowest heaven, and the angels brought near follow it; then likewise from heaven to heaven until he brings it to the seventh heaven, to the Lote-Tree of the Utmost Boundary. There a sealed record from Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, reaches them, in which is a security from Allah for so-and-so son of so-and-so from the punishment of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection, and [the tidings] of winning Paradise. Ibn Zayd said: المقربون are the angels.

nahhas-irab:22-22.t: It was said: they were called أبرار because of the abundance of truthfulness they practise, because truthfulness is called برّ.

nahhas-irab:23-24.t: عَلَى الْأَرائِكِ يَنْظُرُونَ (23), i.e. at the palaces, the ḥūr and other things they have. Abū Jaʿfar said: تَعْرِفُ فِي وُجُوهِهِمْ نَضْرَةَ النَّعِيمِ (24): al-Farrāʾ permitted يُعرف, because it [نضرة] is a non-real feminine.

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: يُسْقَوْنَ مِنْ رَحِيقٍ مَخْتُومٍ (25): مِنْ رَحِيقٍ is in the position of the accusative as the [second] object of the passive verb, not according to the view of al-Akhfash.

nahhas-irab:26-26.t:
خِتامُهُ مِسْكٌ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). This is the reading of most people. Al-Kisāʾī read — Abū ʿUbayd related it from him — «خاتمه مسك», and claimed that this reading is the reading of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him. Ismāʿīl ibn Isḥāq mentioned that he found no one who knew this from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him. [But] it was read [in transmission] to Ibrāhīm ibn Mūsā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm, from Yaḥyā ibn Ziyād, from Muḥammad ibn al-Faḍl, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, that he read «خاتمه مسك». Abū Jaʿfar said: ختامه [and خاتمه] have one meaning, except that ختام is a maṣdar (verbal noun) and خاتم is the active participle. Most of the speech of the Arabs regarding people and the like is "he is their خاتم (seal)", as He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: وَلكِنْ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ وَخاتَمَ النَّبِيِّينَ [al-Aḥzāb: 40], and likewise خاتم; and regarding other than people, ختام, as the poet said: [al-kāmil] 552-
أغلي السّباء بكلّ أدكن عاتق ... أو جونة قدحت وفضّ ختامها
(I pay a high price for wine — every dark, aged [wineskin], or a black jar that is tapped and whose seal is broken.)
وَفِي ذلِكَ فَلْيَتَنافَسِ الْمُتَنافِسُونَ, i.e. let them be eager and seek it. The origin of this is from نفست عليه بالشيء, i.e. I wanted it to be mine rather than his; its derivation is from النّفس, i.e. that in which the soul rejoices and to which it inclines.

nahhas-irab:27-28.t:
عَيْناً يَشْرَبُ بِهَا الْمُقَرَّبُونَ (28): there are five views on the accusative of عين. The view of al-Akhfash is that it is accusative by يسقون. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said — ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān reported it to us — : It is not sound to me that it be accusative except in the sense of أعني ("I mean"). Al-Farrāʾ said: i.e. "from the تسنيم of a spring", then it was given nunation, so it is put in the accusative, like أَوْ إِطْعامٌ فِي يَوْمٍ ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ يَتِيماً ذا مَقْرَبَةٍ [al-Balad: 14]. The fourth view: «تسنيم عينا» [i.e. accusative as tamyīz (specification)]. [Translator's note: the source states the fourth view only as «تسنيم عينا»; the bracketed gloss is an interpretation.] The fifth view is that تسنيم is a definite name of the water and عين is indefinite, so it is accusative for that reason. Abū Jaʿfar said: This view is the closest to correctness, because it is sound according to the view of the exegetes, as Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar read from Ḥafṣ ibn Yūsuf ibn Mūsā [Translator's note: the isnād appears garbled; elsewhere it runs «Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn Ḥafṣ, from Yūsuf ibn Mūsā».]: Salama narrated to us: Nahshal narrated to us from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, who said:
«تسنيم» is a spring that flows down (تتسنّم) from the highest part of Paradise; there is no spring in Paradise nobler than it. Abū Jaʿfar said: The view of Mujāhid also indicates this; he said: تسنيم is height. Likewise the derivation: one says تسنّمت الماء أتسنّمه تسنيما when I made it flow from a high place, and قبر مسنّم means a raised grave; and from this is the camel's hump (سنام). If someone says: Why is تسنيم declined as a triptote when it is definite, a name of something feminine? It is said: its implied form is that it is a masculine name for the water flowing from that high place; and the meaning of عينا is "flowing", so it has come to be in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:29-29.t: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ أَجْرَمُوا, i.e. they earned sin. One says جرم and أجرم when he earned, except that أجرم is more frequent for earning sin, and جرم for other things. الَّذِينَ is the noun (ism) of إنّ; أَجْرَمُوا is its ṣila (relative clause); كانُوا is outside the ṣila because it is the khabar (predicate) of «إن», i.e. they used to be in this world مِنَ الَّذِينَ — those who believed in the oneness of Allah — يَضْحَكُونَ, mocking them. It is related that Abū Jahl and his companions laughed at and mocked ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, and his companions.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t:
The grammarians differed about the position of the hāʾ and mīm [in كالوهم]. Their leading figures — Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, al-Kisāʾī, al-Akhfash and others — said: the position of the hāʾ and mīm is the accusative. This is the school of Sībawayh, by analogy with his saying كلتك ("I measured for you") and صدتك ("I hunted for you"); he does not permit وهبتك, because it is ambiguous, but if you say وهبتك دينارا ("I gave you a dinar") it is permissible. ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar said: the hāʾ and mīm are in the position of the nominative. Abū Ḥātim expressed this by saying that the meaning in his view is: "they, when they measure or weigh, cause loss", because ʿĪsā said: the pause is «وإذا كالوا», then you begin «هم أو وزنوا». Someone else expressed it [by saying] that «هم» is a tawkīd (emphasis), as you say قاموا هم. Abū Jaʿfar said: The correct view is that the hāʾ and mīm are in the position of the accusative, because in the written text (السواد) it is without an alif; and the sequence of the speech indicates that, because before it is إِذَا اكْتالُوا عَلَى النَّاسِ, so what follows must be "and when they measure for them (كالوا لهم)", the lām being omitted, as [the poet] said — Abū Zayd recited it: [al-kāmil] 548-
ولقد جنيتك أكموءا وعساقلا ... ولقد نهيتك عن بنات الأوبر
(I have gathered for you truffles and ʿasāqil, and I forbade you the [inferior] banāt al-awbar.)
The genitive particle is omitted in what takes two objects, one of them by means of a particle, as the poet said: [al-basīṭ] 549-
أمرتك الخير فافعل ما أمرت به ... فقد تركتك ذا مال وذا نشب
(I commanded you to do good, so do what you were commanded, for I have left you possessed of wealth and property.)
Another said: [al-ṭawīl] 550-
نبّيت عبد الله بالجوّ أصبحت ... كراما مواليها لئيما صميمها
(I was told that ʿAbd Allāh, in al-Jaww, has come to have noble clients but base pure-bred members.)
And another said: [al-basīṭ] 551-
أستغفر الله ذنبا لست محصيه ... ربّ العباد إليه الوجه والعمل ]
(I ask Allah's forgiveness for sins I cannot count — the Lord of the servants, to whom [one turns] one's face and deeds.) [Translator's note: a stray bracket appears at the end of the verse in the source.]

nahhas-irab:31-31.t: ] [Translator's note: the entry begins with a stray bracket in the source.] Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās: فاكهين — he is saying: pleased with themselves. Abū Jaʿfar said: That is, pleased with what they were doing and delighted with it. Ibn Zayd said: فاكهين means living in comfort. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that فاكهين [and فكهين] have one meaning. Abū ʿUbayd reported that Abū Zayd al-Anṣārī reported from the Arabs that الفكه is one who laughs much and is good-humoured. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: al-Aṣmaʿī used to extol Abū Zayd in [matters of] language, mentioning his rank and precedence, and mentioning his truthfulness and trustworthiness. He said: And Khalaf ibn Ḥayyān Abū Muḥriz, despite his eminence, used to attend his circle.

nahhas-irab:32-32.t: This is the saying of the disbelievers in this world, i.e. [these] are surely astray from the right path.

nahhas-irab:33-33.t: That is, they were not sent to watch over their deeds; they were only commanded to obey Allah the Exalted.

nahhas-irab:34-36.t: فَالْيَوْمَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنَ الْكُفَّارِ يَضْحَكُونَ (34): that is after they enter Paradise. Ibn ʿAbbās said: Doors to the Fire will be opened for them, and they will look at those who used to mock them in this world and laugh at them; when they see them in the Fire they will rejoice at Allah the Exalted's vengeance on His enemies and laugh at them then, عَلَى الْأَرائِكِ يَنْظُرُونَ (35) at them. Someone else said: on the couches, looking at their palaces and their spouses, and saying to one another: هَلْ ثُوِّبَ الْكُفَّارُ ما كانُوا يَفْعَلُونَ (36). It was also said: هَلْ begins [a new sentence], cut off from what precedes it, i.e. "Have the disbelievers been requited for their deeds?" On this meaning ما is in the position of the accusative.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: أنّ and what it governs are in the position of the two objects.

nahhas-irab:5-6.t:
يَوْمَ يَقُومُ النَّاسُ لِرَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ (6): there are several views on its accusative. The implied form may be "will surely be resurrected on the day people stand before the Lord of the worlds". Al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: it is like your saying الآن ("now"). Al-Farrāʾ made it indeclinable (mabnī).
Abū Jaʿfar said: That is a mistake, making it indeclinable together with the imperfect verb. In Arabic it is permissible to put it in the genitive as a badal (substitute), and in the nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject). This is what there is of i'rab in it. It was read [in transmission] to Bakr ibn Sahl, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūsuf, from ʿĪsā ibn Yūnus, from Ibn ʿAwn, from Ibn ʿUmar, from the Prophet ﷺ, concerning the saying of Allah the Exalted يَوْمَ يَقُومُ النَّاسُ لِرَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ (6): he said: «They will stand in their sweat up to the middle of their ears.» Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a ḥadīth stated in summary form, with a sound chain of transmission. ʿUqba ibn ʿĀmir related it from the Prophet ﷺ in detailed form; he said: «The sun will draw near to the earth on the Day of Resurrection; among people there will be one drowned [in sweat] up to his ankles, one drowned up to the middle of his shins, one drowned up to his shoulders, one drowned up to his neck, one drowned up to the middle of his mouth, bridled by it, and among them one whom the drowning envelops completely.»

nahhas-irab:7-7.t:
Whoever says that كَلَّا is a complete stop (tamām) throughout the Qur'an says: the meaning is "the matter is not as the disbelievers suppose, that they will not be resurrected and will not be punished". The scholars spoke about the meaning of سجّين. Abū Hurayra said: سِجِّينٍ is an open pit in Hell. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: «سجين» is beneath the cheek (خدّ) of Iblīs. [Translator's note: the source reads «حد», read here as «خدّ».] It was said: «سجين» is from السجل ("record"), the nūn being a substitute for the lām, i.e. in what has been written against them. Abū ʿUbayda said: في سجين means "in a prison", and it was said that it is from السجن. Some grammarians said: «سجين» is the rock beneath the lowest earth; he claimed that this is related, and that it is an adjective, because if it were a name of the rock it would be a diptote; he said: and you may make it a name of the stone, so you decline it as a triptote. Abū Jaʿfar said:
The best that has been said about سجين is what is soundly established from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, as was read [in transmission] to Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥajjāj, from Yaḥyā ibn Sulaymān, from Ibn Fuḍayl and Abū Muʿāwiya, from al-Aʿmash, from al-Minhāl, from Zādhān, from al-Barāʾ, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: «When the disbelieving — or the wicked — servant dies, his spirit is taken up to the lowest heaven, and Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, says: Write his record in سِجِّينٍ.» He said:
And it is the lowest earth.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: [وَما أَدْراكَ ما سِجِّينٌ is] for magnification; it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: With an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "it is a written record".

safi-cedvel:1-3.t:
* I'rab:
(ويل) is a nominative mubtadaʾ (subject) [Note: what made it permissible to begin with it is its indicating supplication.] ; (للمطفّفين) is attached to the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; (الذين) is a relative in the position of a genitive, a naʿt (adjective) of المطففين [Note: or it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هم" (they), the nominal sentence being an explanatory resumption.] ; (على الناس) is attached to (اكتالوا) [Note: al-Zamakhsharī said: Since their measuring is a measuring in which they are treated unfairly, (على) was put in place of (من) to indicate that; it is also possible that it is attached to (يستوفون) .] ; (أو) is for conjunction..
Clause: «ويل للمطفّفين ... » has no grammatical position, inceptive.
And the clause: «the condition, its verb and its apodosis ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين) .
And the clause: «اكتالوا ... » is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of a genitive construct).
And the clause: «يستوفون» has no grammatical position, the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
And the clause: «the second condition, its verb and its apodosis» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the first conditional clause.
And the clause: «كالوهم ... » is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «وزنوهم ... » is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the clause كالوهم.
And the clause: «يخسرون» has no grammatical position, the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.

* Morphology:
(المطفّفون): plural of المطفّف, an active participle of the quadriliteral طفّف, on the pattern مفعّل (with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn).
(2) اكتالوا: it has an ʿilāl (weak-letter change) by substitution: the ʿayn of the verb was turned into alif, having been vowelled after a fatḥa; its pattern is افتعلوا.
(يستوفون): it has an ʿilāl by making sākin and an ʿilāl by deletion; its origin is يستوفيون (with a yāʾ after the fāʾ): the vowel of the yāʾ was transferred to the fāʾ because of heaviness, then the yāʾ was deleted because of the meeting of two sākin letters; its pattern is يستفعون.
(3) كالوهم: it has an ʿilāl by substitution, by analogy as in اكتالوا..

* Rhetoric:
Antithesis (al-muqābala): in His saying, the Exalted, «الَّذِينَ إِذَا اكْتالُوا عَلَى النَّاسِ يَسْتَوْفُونَ وَإِذا كالُوهُمْ أَوْ وَزَنُوهُمْ يُخْسِرُونَ» .
That is, the meaning is: when they take from people they take in full, and when they give to them they give short.

* Benefits:
Do not diminish people's things: these verses indicate the severe threat and the painful punishment in the Hereafter for those who shorten measure and weight and cheat people of their rights, while if they are owed a right they take it in full. This threat covers little and much of the cheating of a right. This sin is one of the major sins; whoever does not repent of it is feared to suffer a bad ending. If he repents and returns the rights to their owners, his repentance is accepted; whoever persists in it is persisting in one of the major sins. This is because people at large need transactions, and these are built upon measure, weight and cubit-measurement; for this reason Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made much of the matter of measure and weight. Nāfiʿ said: Ibn ʿUmar used to pass by a seller and say to him: Fear Allah, give full measure and weight, for the cheaters will be made to stand on the Day of Resurrection until their sweat bridles them. Qatāda said: Give in full, son of Adam, as you love to be given in full, and be just as you love to be treated justly. Al-Fuḍayl said: Cheating in the scale is blackness on the Day of Resurrection.

safi-cedvel:4-6.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) is for an interrogative of denial and reproach; (لا) is a negative; (ليوم) is attached to (مبعوثون) ..
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّهم مبعوثون) is in the position of an accusative, standing in place of the two objects of يظنّ.
(يوم) is an accusative adverb of time, attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being يبعثون; (لربّ) is attached to (يقوم) .
Clause: «يظنّ أولئك ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «يقوم الناس ... » is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of a genitive construct).

safi-cedvel:7-9.t:
* I'rab:
(كلّا) is a particle of rebuke and deterrence from what they were doing of cheating in measure and heedlessness of the resurrection; (اللام) is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis; (في سجين) is attached to the khabar (predicate) of إنّ; (الواو) is resumptive; (ما) is an interrogative noun in the position of a nominative, a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar is the clause أدراك; (ما) is like the first, its khabar being (سجّين) ; (كتاب) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هو" (it).
Clause: «إنّ كتاب الفجّار لفي سجّين» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «ما أدراك ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive [Note: or parenthetical, between the first كتاب and the explanatory clause that explains it.]
And the clause: «أدراك ... » is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ما) .
And the clause: «ما سجّين ... » is in the position of an accusative, the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb أدراك.
And the clause: « (هو) كتاب ... » has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption.

* Morphology:
(سجّين): a proper noun either for a book in which the deeds of devils, unbelievers and the wicked are gathered.. or a proper noun for a particular place; its pattern is فعّيل (with kasra on the fāʾ and a doubled ʿayn), taken from السجن ("prison"); it is said that the nūn is a substitute for the lām and the origin is سجّيل, which is derived from السجلّ, meaning "book".
(مرقوم): a passive participle of the triliteral رقم, on the pattern مفعول.

safi-cedvel:10-13.t:
* I'rab:
(ويل ... للمكذّبين) is like ويل للمطفّفين [Note: in verse (1) of the sūra.] ; (يومئذ) is a badal (substitute) for (يوم يقوم) [Note: in verse (6) of this sūra.] ; (الذين) is a relative in the position of a genitive, a naʿt (adjective) of المكذّبين [Note: or the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هم" (they), the nominal sentence being an explanatory resumption.] ; (بيوم) is attached to (يكذّبون) ; (الواو) is circumstantial, or resumptive; (ما) is a negative; (به) is attached to (يكذّب) ; (إلّا) is for restriction; (كلّ) is the nominative fāʿil (agent) of (يكذّب) ; (عليه) is attached to (تتلى) ...
Clause: «ويل ... للمكذّبين» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «يكذّبون ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين) .
And the clause: «ما يكذب به إلّا كلّ ... » is in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl (circumstantial) from يوم الدين [Note: or resumptive, with no grammatical position.] .
And the clause: «the condition, its verb and its apodosis ... » is in the position of a nominative, a naʿt of كلّ معتد.
And the clause: «تتلى عليه آياتنا ... » is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of a genitive construct).
And the clause: «قال ... » has no grammatical position, the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
And the clause: « (هي) أساطير ... » is in the position of an accusative, the quoted speech (maqūl al-qawl).

safi-cedvel:14-14.t:
* I'rab:
(بل) is for a transitional turning-away (iḍrāb intiqālī); (على قلوبهم) is attached to (ران) ; (ما) is a relative noun in the position of a nominative, fāʿil (agent), and the returning pronoun is omitted.
Clause: «ران على قلوبهم ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «كانوا يكسبون ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما) .
And the clause: «يكسبون ... » is in the position of an accusative, the khabar (predicate) of كانوا.

* Morphology:
(ران): it has an ʿilāl (weak-letter change) by substitution; its origin is رين (its imperfect being يرين): the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa and was turned into alif.

safi-cedvel:15-17.t:
* I'rab:
(عن ربّهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (محجوبون), with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "from seeing their Lord", and likewise the adverb (يومئذ) ; the tanwīn is a substitute for a clause, i.e. "the day when the people stand"; (اللام) is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis, in the two places; (ثمّ) is for conjunction in the two places; (الذي) is a relative noun in the position of a nominative, the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (هذا) ; (به) is attached to (تكذّبون) .
Clause: «إنّهم ... لمحجوبون» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «إنّهم لصالوا الجحيم ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive one.
And the clause: «يقال ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive one.
And the clause: «هذا الذي ... » is in the position of a nominative, nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) [Note: it is in origin a clause of quoted speech (maqūl al-qawl).] .
And the clause: «كنتم به تكذّبون» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذي) .
And the clause: «تكذّبون» is in the position of an accusative, the khabar of كنتم.

* Morphology:
(محجوبون): plural of محجوب, a passive participle of the triliteral حجب, on the pattern مفعول.

* Rhetoric:
Simile of representation (al-tamthīl): in His saying, the Exalted, «كَلَّا إِنَّهُمْ عَنْ رَبِّهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ لَمَحْجُوبُونَ» .
Whoever denies that He, the Exalted, can be seen, such as the Muʿtazila, says: the speech is a representation of contempt for them and humiliation of them, because admission to kings is granted only to the esteemed notables in their eyes, and only the lowly and despised are barred from them.

safi-cedvel:18-21.t:
* I'rab:
(كلّها إنّ ... كتاب مرقوم) is like the verse كلّا إنّ ... كتاب مرقوم [Note: in verse (7) of this sūra and those that follow.] ... in its words and clauses.
And the clause: «يشهده المقرّبون ... » is in the position of a nominative, a second khabar (predicate) of the implied mubtadaʾ (subject) (هو) .

* Morphology:
(علّيّون): plural of علّيّ, a derived adjective, on the pattern فعّيل (with kasra on the fāʾ and a doubled ʿayn); or it is a singular in the form of a plural, having no singular from its own wording, its meaning being the book that gathers the good deeds.

* Benefits:
- كلّا:
It is a particle whose meaning is rebuke and deterrence. The grammarians permitted pausing on it and beginning with what follows it. A group said: whenever you hear (كلّا) in a sūra, judge that it is Meccan, because it carries the meaning of threat and warning, and most of that was revealed in Mecca, because most of the insolence was there. This statement is open to question, because كلا sometimes does not carry the meaning of deterrence, as in His saying, the Exalted (ألا يظن أولئك أنهم مبعوثون، ليوم عظيم. يوم يقوم الناس لرب العالمين. كلا إن كتاب الفجار لفي سجّين) .
Al-Kisāʾī, Abū Ḥātim and those who agreed with them held that the meaning of rebuke and deterrence does not continue in it, so they added a second meaning to it, on the basis of which it is correct to pause before it and to begin with it. Then they differed in specifying that meaning, in three views:
1- Al-Kisāʾī and his followers said: it is in the sense of حقا ("truly").
2- Abū Ḥātim and his followers said: it is in the sense of the opening (ألا) .
3- Al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl, al-Farrāʾ and those who agreed with them said: it is a particle of response, equivalent to (إي) and (نعم) , and they interpreted His saying, the Exalted, accordingly: (كلا والقمر) , saying that its meaning is: إي والقمر ("yes, by the moon").
Abū Ḥātim's view is better than their two views, because it is more consistent: أنّ takes kasra after the opening (ألا) but does not take kasra after حقا; and because explaining a particle by a particle is preferable to explaining a particle by a noun. Sometimes (كلا) carries both the meaning of deterrence and the meaning of opening, as in His saying, the Exalted: (رب ارجعون لعلي أعمل صالحا فيما تركت كلا إنها كلمة هو قائلها ومن ورائهم برزخ إلى يوم يبعثون) , because if it were in the sense of حقا, the hamza of إن after it would not take kasra; and if it were in the sense of نعم, it would be a promise to return, because it comes after a request, as when one says (أكرم فلانا) and you answer:
(نعم) .

safi-cedvel:22-28.t:
* I'rab:
(اللام) is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis; (في نعيم) is attached to the khabar (predicate) of إنّ; (على الأرائك) is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of ينظرون; (في وجوههم) is attached to (تعرف) ; (من رحيق) is attached to (يسقون) ; (الواو) is parenthetical; (في ذلك) is attached to the verb (يتنافس) ; (الفاء) connects the apodosis of an omitted conditional; (اللام) is the lām of command; (الواو) is a conjunction; (من تسنيم) is attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (مزاج) ; (عينا) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being أعني ("I mean") or أمدح ("I praise") or يسقون ("they are given to drink"); (بها) is attached to (يشرب) , by its implying the sense of "to be quenched" or "to take delight".
Clause: «إنّ الأبرار لفي نعيم ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «ينظرون ... » is in the position of a nominative, a second khabar «1» .
And the clause: «تعرف ... » is in the position of a nominative, a third khabar «2» .
And the clause: «يسقون ... » is in the position of a nominative, a fourth khabar «3» .
And the clause: «ختامه مسك ... » is in the position of a genitive, a second naʿt (adjective) of رحيق.
And the clause: «ليتنافس المتنافسون ... » is in the position of a jussive, the apodosis of an omitted conditional, i.e. if competition in things is to be completed, let the competitors compete in that.. The omitted conditional clause is parenthetical, with no grammatical position.
And the clause: «مزاجه من تسنيم ... » is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the clause ختامه مسك.
And the clause: «يشرب بها المقرّبون ... » is in the position of an accusative, a naʿt of (عينا) .

* Morphology:
(25) رحيق: a noun for pure wine, on the pattern فعيل.
(مختوم): a passive participle of the triliteral ختم, on the pattern مفعول.
(26) ختامه: either a noun for the thing with which one seals, or a maṣdar (verbal noun) meaning mixing and blending, or meaning "sealing" (with fatḥa on the khāʾ); its pattern is فعال (with kasra on the fāʾ).
(مسك): a noun for a pleasant scent; it is inert (jāmid), on the pattern فعل (with kasra then sukūn).
(المتنافسون): plural of المتنافس, an active participle of the quinqueliteral تنافس, on the pattern متفاعل (with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn).
(27) تسنيم: it is said to be a proper name of a particular spring in Paradise. In origin it is a regular maṣdar of the quadriliteral سنّم, meaning "to raise", or it is used as a maṣdar explained by (عينا) ; its pattern is تفعيل.

safi-cedvel:29-32.t:
* I'rab:
(من الذين) is attached to (يضحكون) ; (بهم) is attached to (مرّوا) ; (إلى أهلهم) is attached to (انقلبوا) ; (فكهين) is an accusative ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of انقلبوا; (اللام) is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis..
Clause: «إنّ الذين أجرموا ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «أجرموا ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين) .
And the clause: «كانوا ... » is in the position of a nominative, the khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
And the clause: «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين) .
And the clause: «يضحكون ... » is in the position of an accusative, the khabar of كانوا..
And the clause: «the condition, its verb and its apodosis ... » is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause يضحكون [Note: or to the clause that is the khabar of انّ: (كانوا ... ) .]
And the clause: «مرّوا ... » is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of a genitive construct).
And the clause: «يتغامزون ... » has no grammatical position, the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
And the clause: «the second condition, its verb and its apodosis ... » is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause يضحكون [Note: or in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause كانوا.. or conjoined to the first clause of the condition, its verb and its apodosis.] .
And the clause: «انقلبوا ... » is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «انقلبوا (the second) ... » has no grammatical position, the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
And the clause: «إذا رأوهم قالوا ... » is in the position of an accusative, or a nominative, conjoined to the preceding clause of the condition, its verb and its apodosis.
And the clause: «رأوهم ... » is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position, the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
And the clause: «إنّ هؤلاء لضالّون ... » is in the position of an accusative, the quoted speech (maqūl al-qawl).

* Morphology:
(31) فكهين: plural of فكه.. a ṣifa mushabbaha (assimilated adjective) from the triliteral فكه (of the bāb of فرح), on the pattern فعل (with fatḥa then kasra).

safi-cedvel:33-33.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is circumstantial; (ما) is a negative; (عليهم) is attached to (حافظين) [Note: the pronoun in (عليهم) refers to the believers.] ; (حافظين) is an accusative ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw in (أرسلوا) .
Clause: «ما أرسلوا ... » is in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent) of قالوا.

safi-cedvel:34-36.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) connects the apodosis of an omitted conditional; (اليوم) is an adverb of time attached to the upcoming (يضحكون) ; (من الكفار) is attached to the (يضحكون) after it; (على الأرائك) is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of ينظرون [Note: and see verse (23) of this sūra.] ; (هل) is an interrogative particle; (ما) is a maṣdar (verbal noun) particle [Note: or a relative noun in the position of an accusative by removal of the preposition.. and the returning pronoun is omitted.] ..
The interpreted maṣdar (ما كانوا ... ) is in the position of an accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e.: مما كانوا ...
Clause: «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين) .
And the clause: «الذين آمنوا ... » is in the position of a jussive, the apodosis of an omitted conditional, i.e.: if those who committed crimes laughed at those who believed in the world, then those who believed laugh today at the unbelievers.
And the clause: «يضحكون ... » is in the position of a nominative, the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (الذين) .
And the clause: «ينظرون ... » is in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl from the fāʿil of يضحكون.
And the clause: «ثوّب الكفّار ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive [Note: or it is in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb of looking suspended by the interrogative, with the preposition implied.. and it is said that it is in the position of an accusative as quoted speech of an implied saying, i.e.: the believers say to one another: have the unbelievers been repaid ...] .

semin-durr:11-11.t: His saying: {الذين يُكَذِّبُونَ}: it may follow [the preceding noun] (itbāʿ) as a naʿt (adjective), a badal (substitute) or a bayān (explicative apposition), or it may be cut off (qaṭʿ), in the nominative or the accusative.

semin-durr:13-13.t: His saying: {إِذَا}: the majority read it as a statement. Al-Ḥasan read «أإذا» as a disapproving (inkārī) question. The majority read «تُتْلى» with two dotted-above tāʾs, while Abū Ḥaywa and Ibn Miqsam read it with the yāʾ dotted below, because the feminine gender is metaphorical (majāzī).

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying: {بَلْ رَانَ}: Ḥafṣ's pause on «بل» was discussed earlier in al-Kahf. Al-rayn and al-rān are a covering over the heart, like rust on a polished thing such as a sword, a mirror and the like. The poet said:
4515 - وكم رانَ مِنْ ذنبٍ على قلبِ فاجِرٍ ... فتابَ مِن الذنبِ الذي ران وانْجَلَى
(How many a sin has covered the heart of a sinner, and then he repented of the sin that covered it, and it cleared away.)
The original meaning of al-rayn is overpowering (al-ghalaba); from it comes: "the wine overpowered (rānat) the mind of its drinker", and "the swoon overpowered the mind of the sick man". The poet said:
4516 -. . . . . . . . . . . . رانَتْ به الخَمْ ... رُ. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(… the wine overpowered him …)
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "One says: rāna ʿalayhi al-dhanbu and ghāna [the sin covered him], with the maṣdars (verbal nouns) raynan and ghaynan. Al-ghayn is cloud (al-ghaym). One says: rāna fīhi al-nawm, i.e. sleep became firmly settled in him; and rānat bihi al-khamr, i.e. the wine carried him off." Abū Zayd reported: "rīna bi-l-rajuli raynan [the man was overcome]", so its maṣdar comes with the middle radical both with fatḥa and with sukūn. And «ما كانوا» is the fāʿil (agent). «ما» may be maṣdariyya, or it may mean "that which" (alladhī), with the returning pronoun omitted. The alif of «ران» was read both with imāla (inclination) and with tafkhīm (full a-sound): the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] and Abū Bakr read it with imāla, and the rest with tafkhīm. The lām of «بل» was both assimilated into the rāʾ and pronounced distinctly.

semin-durr:15-15.t: His saying: {عَن رَّبِّهِمْ}: it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the khabar (predicate), and so is «يومئذٍ». The tanwīn [in يومئذ] compensates for a clause whose implied form is: "on the day when people stand", because nothing else would fit as its implied form.

semin-durr:17-17.t: His saying: {يُقَالُ}: what stands in place of the agent [i.e. the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)] may be what is indicated by the clause in his saying {هذا الذي كُنتُمْ}; it may be the clause itself; and it may be the maṣdar (verbal noun). This was set out in detail at the beginning of al-Baqara.

semin-durr:18-18.t: His saying: {لَفِي عِلِّيِّينَ}: it is the khabar (predicate) of «إنَّ». Ibn ʿAṭiyya said here just what he said there, and he is answered with what was said before. ʿIlliyyūn is the plural of ʿilliyy, or it is the name of a place in the highest part of Paradise, and it has been treated like the plural of rational beings, so it takes wāw in the nominative and yāʾ in the accusative and genitive, although the condition of rationality is not met. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Its singular is ʿilliyy, which is the angel. It has also been said: it is a plural form like ʿishrūn (twenty)"; then he mentioned something similar to what he mentioned regarding «سِجِّين» concerning the omission mentioned before. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "ʿIlliyyūn is a proper name (ʿalam) for the register of good in which is recorded everything that the angels and the righteous among humans and jinn have done; it is transferred from the plural of ʿilliyy, of the pattern fiʿʿīl from al-ʿuluww (height), like «سِجِّين» from al-sijn (prison). It was so named either because it is the cause of elevation, or because it is raised up in the seventh heaven." I say: all the views given earlier on «سِجِّين» apply here as well.

semin-durr:21-21.t: His saying: {يَشْهَدُهُ}: a clause which may be a second ṣifa (adjective), or may be resumptive (mustaʾnafa).

semin-durr:24-24.t:
His saying: {تَعْرِفُ}: the majority read it with the verb ascribed to the one addressed, i.e. "you recognise", O Muhammad, or anyone capable of recognising.
Abū Jaʿfar, Ibn Abī Isḥāq, Shayba, Ṭalḥa, Yaʿqūb and al-Zaʿfarānī read «تُعْرَفُ» in the passive, with «نَضْرَةُ» in the nominative as standing in place of the agent (nāʾib fāʿil). ʿAlī ibn Zayd read likewise, except with the yāʾ below, because the feminine gender is metaphorical.
[And his saying {يَنظُرُونَ} is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in the khabar, or it is resumptive.] [And «على الأرائك» is attached to «يَنْظرون», or is a ḥāl from its pronoun, or is a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in the khabar.]

semin-durr:25-25.t:
His saying: {مِن رَّحِيقٍ}: al-raḥīq is a drink in which there is no adulteration; it has also been said: the finest wine. Ḥassān said:
4517 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... بَرَدى يُصَفِّقُ بالرَّحيقِ السَّلْسَلِ
(… [the water of] Baradā mixed with pure, smooth-flowing wine.)

semin-durr:26-26.t:
His saying: {خِتَامُهُ}: al-Kisāʾī read «خاتَمهُ», with fatḥa on the tāʾ after the alif; the rest read it with the tāʾ before the alif. The rationale of al-Kisāʾī's reading is that he made it a noun for that with which the cup is sealed, as shown by his saying «مَخْتوم» (sealed); then He made clear what the seal is. It is also reported from al-Kisāʾī that he read the tāʾ with kasra, so it would be like the saying of the Exalted: {وَخَاتَمَ النبيين} [al-Aḥzāb: 40]; the meaning is: a seal whose scent is musk. The rationale of the reading of the majority is that al-khitām is the clay with which a thing is sealed, and musk was put in its place. The poet said:
4518 - كأنَّ مُشَعْشَعاً مِنْ خَمْرِ بُصْرى ... . . . . . . البُخْتُ مَسْدودَ الخِتامِ
(As if diluted wine of Buṣrā … the Bactrian camels [carried], its seal stopped up.)
It has also been said: [khitām is] its blend and its mixture. It has also been said: its ending, i.e. the end of drinking it, in which a person finds the scent of musk. Al-tanāfus (vying) is contending for a precious (nafīs) thing. One says: nafistu bihi nafāsatan, i.e. I was miserly with it. Its origin is from al-nafs (the soul), because of its preciousness.

semin-durr:27-27.t: His saying: {مِن تَسْنِيمٍ}: tasnīm is the name of a spring in Paradise. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Tasnīm is a proper name (ʿalam) for a particular spring, named with tasnīm, which is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of sanamahu, when one raises it." I say: there is a difficulty in this, because it ought then to have been a diptote (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf) owing to being a proper name and feminine, even if the feminine is metaphorical. Its being masculine in origin does not detract from that, because what counts is its state as a proper name: do you not see that they state explicitly that if a woman were named Zayd it would have to be a diptote, even though in «هِنْد» there are two options? Unless you say: it was treated in the manner of Hind and the like, so it would be like Wāsiṭ and Dābiq.

semin-durr:28-28.t: His saying: {عَيْناً}: there are several views on it. First: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial); al-Zajjāj said this, meaning from «تَسْنيم», because it is a proper name for a particular thing — except that it is problematic because it is a non-derived (jāmid) noun. Second: it is accusative by way of praise; al-Zamakhsharī said this. Third: it is accusative through an implied «يُسْقَونْ» (they are given to drink); al-Akhfash said this. As for his saying «يَشْرب» بها: i.e. from it; or the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida); or «يَشْربُ» is made to include the meaning of "to quench one's thirst" (yarwī). This was discussed fully in Sūrat al-Insān.

semin-durr:29-29.t: His saying: {َمِنَ الذين آمَنُواْ}: attached to «يَضْحكون», i.e. on account of them; it was put first for the sake of the verse-endings (fawāṣil). Al-taghāmuz is signalling with the eye.

semin-durr:31-31.t: His saying: {فَكِهِينَ}: Ḥafṣ read «فَكِهين» without an alif, and the rest with it. It has been said: the two have the same meaning. It has also been said: fakihīn means insolent, and fākihīn is from al-tafakkuh (jesting). It has also been said: fakihīn means rejoicing, and fākihīn means living in comfort. It has also been said: fākihīn means people of fruit and jest.

semin-durr:32-32.t: His saying: {وَإِذَا رَأَوْهُمْ}: the nominative [pronoun] may refer to the disbelievers and the accusative one to the believers, and the reverse is also possible; and likewise the two pronouns in «أُرْسِلوا عليهم».

semin-durr:34-34.t: His saying: {فاليوم}: accusative through «يَضْحَكون». Its being placed before the mubtadaʾ (subject) does no harm, because if the governing word were placed first here it would be permissible, since there is no ambiguity — unlike «زيدٌ قام في الدار», for which one may not say: في الدار زيدٌ قام.

semin-durr:35-35.t: His saying: {عَلَى الأرآئك يَنظُرُونَ}: as was said on its parallel.

semin-durr:36-36.t:
His saying: {هَلْ ثُوِّبَ}: the interrogative clause may suspend (tuʿalliq) the "looking" before it, so it would be in the position of the accusative after the preposition is dropped. It may also be on the implication of an omitted verb of saying, i.e. "they say: have [the disbelievers] been repaid?". Thuwwiba means: was recompensed. One says: thawwabahu and athābahu. The poet said:
4519 - سَأَجْزِيك أو يَجْزيك عني مُثَوِّبٌ ... وحَسْبُك أَنْ يُثْنَى عليك وتُحْمَدَا
(I shall repay you, or a rewarder will repay you on my behalf; and it is enough for you to be praised and lauded.)
Abū ʿAmr, al-Kisāʾī and Ḥamza assimilated the lām of «هل» into the thāʾ. In his saying «ما كانوا» there is an omission, i.e. "the reward of what they used to [do]". And «ما» is a nominal relative or a particle relative (i.e. maṣdariyya).

semin-durr:9-9.t:
Al-raqm means writing (al-khaṭṭ). It has also been said: sealing (al-khatm), in the dialect of Ḥimyar; but the first is correct. The poet said:
4514 - سأَرْقُمُ في الماءِ القَراح إليكُمُ ... على بُعْدِكُمْ إنْ كان للماءِ راقِمُ
(I shall write to you on clear water, despite your distance, if water could ever be written upon.)
This root was discussed earlier in al-Kahf.

semin-durr:1-1.t:
His saying: {وَيْلٌ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject); what justified beginning with it [though indefinite] is its being an imprecation. Had it been accusative, it would have been permissible. Makkī said: "The preferred form for «وَيْل» and the like, when not in iḍāfa (genitive construct), is the nominative, and the accusative is permissible. If it is in iḍāfa or made definite, the preferred form / is the accusative, as in {وَيْلَكُمْ لاَ تَفْتَرُواْ} [Ṭā Hā: 61]." «للمُطَفِّفين» is its khabar (predicate).
Al-muṭaffif is the one who gives short measure. Its real meaning is taking, in measure or weight, something ṭafīf, i.e. scanty and paltry; from it is their saying "below the ṭafīf", i.e. the trifling thing, because of its smallness.

semin-durr:2-2.t: His saying: {عَلَى الناس}: There are several views concerning it. The first: that it is attached to «اكْتالوا», «على» and «مِنْ» alternating here. Al-Farrāʾ said: "One says iktaltu ʿalā al-nās: I took full measure from them; and iktaltu minhum: I took what they owed." It was also said: «على» means «مِنْ»; one says iktaltu ʿalayhi and minhu with one meaning; but the first is clearer. It was also said: «على» is attached to «يَسْتَوْفُون». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Since their taking by measure was a taking by measure that harmed [the people] and in which [the people] were wronged, He put «على» in place of «مِنْ» to indicate that. It may also be attached to «يَسْتَوْفون», the object being placed before the verb to convey specificity, i.e. they take full measure against people specifically; as for themselves, they take full measure for them." End of quotation. And it is good.

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying: {كَالُوهُمْ أَوْ وَّزَنُوهُمْ}: They were written in the codex without an alif after the wāw in both verbs; for this reason people disagreed about «هم» in two ways. The first: it is an accusative pronoun, so it is a direct object and refers to the people, i.e. when they measure for the people or weigh for the people. On this view these two verbs in origin take two objects, one directly without disagreement and the other by means of a preposition, which may be deleted. Whether each of the two [constructions] is original in itself, or one of them is the origin of the other, is a well-known disagreement. The implied form is: when they measure food for them or weigh it for them; then the preposition and the free object were deleted. Al-Zamakhsharī recited:
4513 - ولقد جَنَيْتُكَ أَكْمُؤاً وعَساقِلاً ... ولقد نَهْيْتُك عَن بناتِ الأَوْبَرِ
(I have gathered you truffles and white truffles, and I have forbidden you the inferior small truffles.)
i.e. gathered for you. The second: that it is a nominative pronoun emphasising the wāw, the pronoun referring to the defrauders; on this view the thing measured and the one for whom it is measured, and the thing weighed and the one for whom it is weighed, have all been omitted. However, al-Zamakhsharī rejected this and said: "It is not valid for it to be a nominative pronoun for the defrauders, because the speech would thereby turn into a corrupt arrangement. That is, the meaning is: when they take from people they take in full, and when they give to them they cause loss. If you make the pronoun refer to the defrauders, it turns into your saying: when they take from people they take in full, and when they themselves in particular undertake the measuring or weighing they cause loss; and this is incoherent speech, because the discourse is about the act, not about the one performing it."
The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "There is no incoherence in it in any way, and there is no difference between emphasising the pronoun or not; the discourse is about the act. The most that is in this is that what taking in full is attached to, namely «على الناس», is mentioned, while in {كَالُوهُمْ أَوْ وَّزَنُوهُمْ} it is omitted because it is known, since it is known that they do not cause loss to themselves." I say: al-Zamakhsharī wants to preserve that the meaning is tied to two things: when they take from others, and when they give to others; and this is complete only on the supposition that the pronoun is accusative referring to the people, not that it is a nominative pronoun referring to the defrauders. There is no doubt that this meaning which al-Zamakhsharī mentioned and intended is more complete and better than the second meaning. The first is preferred by the absence of the alif after the wāw, since that indicates the pronoun's being attached. However, al-Zamakhsharī made a qualification, saying: "Relying, in invalidating it, on the script of the codex and on the alif written after the wāw of the plural not being present in it is feeble, because the script of the codex in much of it did not observe the norm agreed upon in the science of writing. Besides, I have seen in books written by the hands of meticulous imams this alif rejected, because it has no reality in either pronunciation or meaning, since the wāw alone gives the meaning of the plural. This alif was written only to distinguish between the wāw of the plural and others in forms like your saying «هم [لم] يَدْعُوا» and «هو يَدْعُو»; whoever did not write it said: the meaning suffices to distinguish between them. It is reported from ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and Ḥamza that they adopted that, i.e. they made the two pronouns refer to the defrauders, and paused at the two wāws a slight pause by which they made clear what they intended."
He did not mention the act of weighing first; rather, He restricted Himself to measuring and said «إذا اكْتالوا», and did not say "or took by weight", as He said the second time «أو وَزَنُوهم». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is as though the defrauders used to take what is measured and weighed only by measures, not by scales, because by taking by measure they were able to take in full and to steal, since they would shake [the measure] and use tricks in filling it; and when they gave, / they measured and weighed, because they were able to cheat in both kinds."
His saying «يُخْسِرون» is the apodosis (jawāb) of «إذا», and it is made transitive by the hamza. One says: the man khasira (lost), and I akhsartuhu (made him lose); so its object is omitted, i.e. they make people lose their goods.

semin-durr:4-4.t: His saying: {أَلا يَظُنُّ}: The apparent view is that it is the «ألا» of urging (taḥḍīḍ): He urged them to that, and «الظنّ» then means certainty. It was also said: it is the negating «لا» with the interrogative hamza entering it.

semin-durr:6-6.t: His saying: {يَوْمَ يَقُومُ}: It may be accusative by «مَبْعُوثون», as al-Zamakhsharī said; or by an implied «يُبْعَثون»; or as a badal (substitute) for the position of «يوم»; or by an implied «أَعْني»; or it is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject); or genitive as a badal for «ليومٍ عظيمٍ». In these last two aspects it was only made indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa because of its iḍāfa (genitive construct) to the verb, even though [the verb] is imperfect, as is the view of the Kufans. What indicates the soundness of these two aspects is the reading of Zayd ibn ʿAlī «يومُ يقومُ» in the nominative, and what Abū Muʿādh the reader related: «يوم» in the genitive, according to what has preceded.

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying: {لَفِي سِجِّينٍ}: They disagreed about the nūn of «سِجِّين». It was said: it is radical; its derivation is from al-sijn, which is imprisonment, and it is an intensive form; so sijjīn is from al-sajn as sikkīr is from al-sukr. It was also said: rather, it is a replacement for lām, the origin being sijjīl, derived from al-sijill, which is a written record. They also disagreed about it: is it the name of a place or the name of a specific book? And is it an adjective, or a proper name transferred from an adjective, like Ḥātim? It is fully declinable (maṣrūf), since there is only one cause [of diptosis] in it, namely being a proper name. If it is the name of a place, then His saying «كتابٌ مَرْقُوْمٌ» is either a badal (substitute) for it, or the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), which is a pronoun referring to it. On both assumptions it is problematic, because the book is not the place. So it was said: the implied form is "it is the place of a book", and then the muḍāf was deleted. It was also said: the implied form is "And what will make you know what the book of sijjīn is?" So the deletion is either from the first or from the second. If, however, we say that it is the name of a book, there is no problem.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Whoever says that sijjīn is a place, then «كتابٌ» is nominative as the khabar of «إنّ», and the adverbial phrase «لفي سِجِّين» is non-operative (mulghā); and whoever makes it an expression for loss, then «كتابٌ» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, the implied form being 'it is a book', and this speech explains what sijjīn is." End of quotation. This is not valid at all, since the entry of the lām determines that it is the khabar, so it cannot be non-operative. It cannot be said: the lām enters what the khabar governs, and this is of that kind, so it is non-operative; because if the khabar, namely «كتابٌ», were supposed to govern, or its adjective «مرقوم» to govern, that would be impossible. As for «كتابٌ» being prevented from governing, it is because it is qualified, and a qualified maṣdar (verbal noun) does not govern. As for «مرقومٌ» being prevented from governing, it is because it is an adjective, and what an adjective governs does not precede the noun it qualifies. Moreover, the lām enters what the khabar governs only under its condition, and this is not governed by the khabar. So it is determined that the preposition-phrase is the khabar and is not non-operative. As for his second statement, "and this speech explains what sijjīn is", it is problematic, because the book is not the loss to which the pronoun was made to refer, being informed about by «كتابٌ».
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: Allah the Exalted has informed about the book of the wicked that it is in sijjīn, and has explained sijjīn by «كتاب مرقوم», so it is as though it were said: their book is in a written book—what then is its meaning? I say: «سِجِّين» is a comprehensive book; it is the register of evil in which Allah has recorded the deeds of the devils and the deeds of the unbelievers and the wicked among jinn and men. It is a book inscribed, clear in its writing, or marked, so that whoever sees it knows that there is no good in it. So the meaning is that what is written of the deeds of the wicked is recorded in that register. It is called sijjīl «[Translator's note: so in the text; the context indicates «سِجِّيناً» (sijjīn)]», of the pattern fiʿʿīl, from al-sajl «[Translator's note: so in the text; the context indicates «السَّجْن» (al-sajn)]», which is imprisonment and constriction, because it is the cause of imprisonment and constriction in Hell." End of quotation.

ukberi-tibyan:3-3.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذَا كَالُوهُمْ أَوْ وَزَنُوهُمْ يُخْسِرُونَ (٣)).
The words of the Exalted (كَالُوهُمْ): there are two views on «هُمْ». First: it is an attached object pronoun, and the implied form is «كَالُوا لَهُمْ» (they measured for them).
It is also said that this verb is sometimes transitive by itself and sometimes through a preposition, and the object here is omitted, i.e. «كَالُوهُمُ الطَّعَامَ» (they measured out the food for them) and the like. On this view «كَالُوا» and «وَزَنُوا» are not written with the alif.
The second view: it is a detached pronoun emphasising the agent pronoun; on this view the two are written with the alif.

ukberi-tibyan:4-4.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَلَا يَظُنُّ أُولَئِكَ أَنَّهُمْ مَبْعُوثُونَ (٤)).
The words of the Exalted (أَلَا يَظُنُّ): the origin is the negating (لَا), which the interrogative hamza has entered; it is not the (أَلَا) of drawing attention (tanbīh), because what follows that one is affirmative, whereas here it is negated.

ukberi-tibyan:5-7.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لِيَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ (٥) يَوْمَ يَقُومُ النَّاسُ لِرَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ (٦) كَلَّا إِنَّ كِتَابَ الْفُجَّارِ لَفِي سِجِّينٍ (٧)).
The words of the Exalted (يَوْمَ يَقُومُ النَّاسُ): it is a badal (substitute) for the position of the preposition and its genitive noun.
It is also said that the implied form is «يُبْعَثُونَ يَوْمَ يَقُومُ النَّاسُ» (they will be resurrected on the day mankind stands). It is also said that the implied form is «أَعْنِي» (I mean). It is also said that it is indeclinable (mabnī), and properly it should be genitive or nominative. The nūn in «سِجِّين» is a root letter, from «السِّجْن», which is imprisonment.
It is also said that it is a substitute for a lām.

ukberi-tibyan:9-9.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (كِتَابٌ مَرْقُومٌ (٩)).
The words of the Exalted (كِتَابٌ): i.e. it is the place of a book, because «السِّجِّين» is a place.
It is also said that the implied form is «هُوَ كِتَابٌ» (it is a book), without [any further] omission, the implied form [of the preceding] being: «وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا كِتَابُ سِجِّينٍ» (and what will make you know what the book of Sijjīn is).

ukberi-tibyan:17-19.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ثُمَّ يُقَالُ هَذَا الَّذِي كُنْتُمْ بِهِ تُكَذِّبُونَ (١٧) كَلَّا إِنَّ كِتَابَ الْأَبْرَارِ لَفِي عِلِّيِّينَ (١٨) وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا عِلِّيُّونَ (١٩)).
The words of the Exalted (ثُمَّ يُقَالُ): what stands in place of the agent (nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent) is a latent pronoun, explained by the clause after it. It is also said that it is the clause itself. As for «عِلِّيُّونَ», its singular is «عِلِّيّ», which is «الْمُلْك» (dominion). [Translator's note: so vocalised in the text; some sources read «الْمَلَك» (the angel).]
It is also said that it is a plural form like «عِشْرِين» (twenty) with no singular, and the implied form is: «عِلِّيُّونَ مَحَلُّ كِتَابٍ» (ʿIlliyyūn is the place of a book). It is also said that the implied form is: «مَا كِتَابُ عِلِّيِّينَ» (what is the book of ʿIlliyyīn).

ukberi-tibyan:23-23.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (عَلَى الْأَرَائِكِ يَنْظُرُونَ (٢٣)).
(يَنْظُرُونَ) is a naʿt (adjective) of «الْأَبْرَار»; it may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial), or resumptive (mustaʾnaf).
«عَلَى» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to it. It may also be a ḥāl, either from the pronoun in the genitive phrase before it, or from the agent in «يَنْظُرُونَ».

ukberi-tibyan:28-28.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (عَيْنًا يَشْرَبُ بِهَا الْمُقَرَّبُونَ (٢٨)).
The words of the Exalted (عَيْنًا): i.e. «أَعْنِي عَيْنًا» (I mean a spring). It is also said that the implied form is «يُسْقَوْنَ عَيْنًا» (they are given to drink a spring), i.e. the water of a spring.
It is also said that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (تَسْنِيمٍ), «تَسْنِيمٍ» being a proper name. It is also said that «تَسْنِيمٍ» is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and it is what makes «عَيْنًا» accusative. (يَشْرَبُ بِهَا) has been discussed in [Sūrat] al-Insān.

ukberi-tibyan:36-36.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (هَلْ ثُوِّبَ الْكُفَّارُ مَا كَانُوا يَفْعَلُونَ (٣٦)).
The words of the Exalted (هَلْ ثُوِّبَ): the clause is in an accusative position by «يَنْظُرُونَ».
It is also said that it has no position. It is also said that the implied form is: «يُقَالُ لَهُمْ: هَلْ ثُوِّبَ» (it will be said to them: have [the disbelievers] been repaid). And Allah knows best.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Muṭaffifīn
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَيْلٌ لِلْمُطَفِّفِينَ﴾: «وَيْلٌ» is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is His saying ﴿لِلْمُطَفِّفِينَ﴾. Were it outside the Qur'an, «وَيْلًا لِلْمُطَفِّفِينَ» would be permissible, in the sense "Allah has appointed woe for them"; but the nominative is better in the reading, because the meaning is: "this has become established for them." «اَلْوَيْلُ» is a word said of everyone who is in punishment and perdition. «اَلْمُطَفِّفُونَ» are those who give short measure and weight. The doer of this is called «مُطَفِّفٌ» only because he hardly steals in measure and weight anything but a trifling, slight (ṭafīf) thing; it is taken from «طَفُّ الشَّيْءِ», which is its edge. He explained their matter in the sūra, saying: ﴿الَّذِينَ إذا اكْتالُوا عَلى النّاسِ يَسْتَوْفُونَ﴾ [al-Muṭaffifīn: 2]; the meaning is: "when they take measure from people, they exact the full measure from them, and likewise when they take weight they exact the full weight."
